condition: Panchakarma: Ayurveda's classical five-procedure cleansing programme (Vamanam, Virechan, Vasti, Nasyam, Raktamokshana). It is a programme, not one disease. The page aims it at people with persistent digestive complaints, chronic joint problems or metabolic issues, and at anyone seeking "systemic renewal". The programme page sells it as a stay of at least 14 nights, priced per villa per night.

proofreading.quote: recognized for permanently resolving disease and restoring systemic balance
proofreading.problem: This claims permanent resolution of disease, which is a cure claim in all but the banned word. It is not supportable and exposes the business on GST and clinical grounds. It is in the first paragraph a patient reads.
proofreading.fix: Replace with physician-approved wording, e.g. "a classical Ayurvedic cleansing programme that aims to restore balance; your physician will explain what to expect for your condition". Needs Dr. Deepu John's sign-off.

proofreading.quote: 80% guest-trusted scientific detox for body, mind, and dosha balance | 30,000+ Lives Transformed
proofreading.problem: Contains the banned word "guest". "80% guest-trusted" means nothing, and "scientific detox" and "30,000+ Lives Transformed" have no source. The same string is the og:title, so it appears on every social share.
proofreading.fix: Use a factual line, e.g. "Physician-supervised Panchakarma at an NABH-accredited Ayurvedic hospital". Keep a number only if the owner supplies its source (HARD GATE 6). Fix the og:title too.

proofreading.quote: 87% of guests report dramatic health improvement within two weeks. 94% maintain benefits long-term
proofreading.problem: Outcome percentages with no source, method or year. Also uses the banned word "guests". This line appears only on this page.
proofreading.fix: Remove unless the owner provides an audited data source and Dr. Deepu John approves the wording. If kept, say "patients" and cite the source.

proofreading.quote: Zero adverse reactions in 100,000+ therapies—safe, expert clinical care
proofreading.problem: An absolute safety claim with no source. It contradicts /faqs-downloads/, which says some patients get mild detoxification symptoms such as headaches, fatigue or digestive changes. Induced emesis and purgation are strong bodily reactions by design.
proofreading.fix: Remove. Replace with an honest monitoring statement, e.g. "Your physician monitors you daily and adjusts treatment if you feel unwell" (physician to approve).

proofreading.quote: 92% patient satisfaction among international clients (2024 data)
proofreading.problem: A statistic with no named survey, sample size or source. The same figure appears on 3 programme pages. The /online-consultation/ page says the hospital does not publish curated quotes and sends readers to Google reviews, so the two pages take opposite positions.
proofreading.fix: Cite the survey (owner) or remove it and link to the public Google reviews, as /online-consultation/ does.

proofreading.quote: Drawing on 5,000 years of Ayurveda wisdom, Panchakarma is the gold standard for natural detoxification and rejuvenation.
proofreading.problem: "Gold standard" is a superlative clinical claim. "5,000 years" contradicts /faqs-downloads/, which says Ayurveda's "texts date back over two thousand years".
proofreading.fix: e.g. "Panchakarma is Ayurveda's classical five-part cleansing programme, described in texts over two thousand years old." The owner should pick one antiquity figure for the whole site.

proofreading.quote: Panchakarma might last anywhere from seven to twenty-one days.
proofreading.problem: The FAQ's duration contradicts this page ("requiring a minimum two-week commitment"; "Villas — Minimum Duration is 14 Nights") and /faqs-downloads/ ("Panchakarma & Detoxification — from 14 nights"). A patient can't tell whether 7 nights is allowed. The same text is in the FAQPage JSON-LD.
proofreading.fix: Physician or owner to set the rule, e.g. "Panchakarma at Kairali runs for a minimum of 14 nights; your physician may advise 21 nights for your condition." Change the accordion and the JSON-LD together.

proofreading.quote: Internal herbal medicines, lab tests, or specialty therapies (e.g., Panchakarma) available as needed.
proofreading.problem: On the Panchakarma package page itself, Panchakarma is listed as an extra-cost add-on. The patient cannot tell whether the nightly rate includes the procedures they are booking for. This is shared template copy found on 31 pages.
proofreading.fix: Owner to state what this package includes, e.g. "Your Panchakarma procedures are included; internal medicines and lab tests are charged as prescribed." Remove the "(e.g., Panchakarma)" example on this page.

proofreading.quote: All-Inclusive Pricing: No hidden fees! Includes accommodation, meals, therapies, and applicable taxes.
proofreading.problem: Contradicts the same page: "Internal Medicines and test reports ... will cost extra", "Additional food items will be charged separately", and laundry, telephone and internet are charged extra.
proofreading.fix: Drop "All-Inclusive" and "No hidden fees!". Instead list what the price covers and what is charged separately.

proofreading.quote: Internal Medicines and test reports needed for your treatment can only be ascertained as your treatment progresses and will cost extra.
proofreading.problem: Contradicts /faqs-downloads/, which lists "Herbal medicines and formulations during your stay" as included in the package. No typical cost range is given either.
proofreading.fix: Owner to decide whether medicines are included or extra, and align both pages. If extra, give an indicative range (needs owner).

proofreading.quote: Support: Airport transfers & multilingual staff
proofreading.problem: Listed under Inclusions, which implies transfers are free. /faqs-downloads/ charges for them (Coimbatore Airport ₹6,775 MPV, one way). "Multilingual" does not say which languages.
proofreading.fix: "Airport transfers can be arranged at extra cost (see How to Reach). Languages spoken: [owner to list]."

proofreading.quote: The above rates are valid from April 1, 2025, to October 31, 2026.
proofreading.problem: /faqs-downloads/ quotes different current rates ("valid 1 Oct 2026 – 30 Sep 2027"), and the two windows overlap in October 2026. As of 23 Sep 2026 these tariffs expire in about 5 weeks, and no price is shown for a November admission.
proofreading.fix: Owner to confirm the 2026–27 tariff and validity, then update this page and the price-list PDFs.

proofreading.quote: Led by 5th-generation Ayurvedic physicians, each treatment is reviewed for maximum safety and efficacy.
proofreading.problem: Contradicts /faqs-downloads/, where the family "represents four generations". The physicians named on /online-consultation/ are BAMS physicians, not generations of the family.
proofreading.fix: e.g. "Led by BAMS-qualified physicians under Chief Physician Dr. Deepu John". Owner to confirm the generation count.

proofreading.quote: My inflammatory markers dropped 65% within 21 days, and I discontinued three medication courses.
proofreading.problem: A lab result plus stopping medication: this reads as advice to come off medicines. The quote, attributed to "Sarah M., Germany", appears word for word on /personalized-customized-healing-program/ and sits next to a video of a bearded man. Its authenticity and consent cannot be verified.
proofreading.fix: Remove unless the owner produces the patient's consent and source. Never publish claims that a patient stopped medication.

proofreading.quote: They found issues missed by Western medicine. I am symptom-free after three weeks.

proofreading.quote: It enhances immunity, digestion, and general health.

proofreading.fix: e.g. "It aims to support digestion and overall wellbeing; your physician will explain what to expect for your condition." Fix the accordion and the JSON-LD.

objectionGaps.question: Which of the five procedures will I actually have: all of them, including induced vomiting, purgation, medicated enemas and Raktamokshana (blood-letting), or only the ones my physician chooses?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The Process section presents all five as "the following steps" of the programme. A 60-year-old reading "controlled emesis" and an unexplained "Raktamokshana" assumes the worst and does not book.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner: Dr. Deepu John to state which procedures KTAHV performs, how they are selected, and whether blood-letting or leech therapy is offered

objectionGaps.question: I take blood-pressure, diabetes, thyroid, statin or blood-thinner medication. Can I keep taking it through the purgation and emesis days, and who adjusts my doses?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Emesis and purgation cause fluid and electrolyte shifts and can change how pills are absorbed. The page's own testimonial suggests stopping medicines, which frightens careful patients and their GPs.
objectionGaps.answerSource: The principle is on /online-consultation/ ("never stop a prescribed medicine without their guidance"). The Panchakarma-specific protocol needs physician/owner. The medication FAQ on /personalized-customized-healing-program/ needs physician verification before reuse.

objectionGaps.question: Am I too old or too unwell for Panchakarma? Who should not have it (heart disease, pacemaker, kidney disease, osteoporosis, recent surgery, cancer treatment, pregnancy)?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: FAQ 3 says it suits "the majority of people" but never names who is excluded. A patient over 60 with other conditions needs to know before paying for flights.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (no stated maximum age; senior-patient considerations). The contraindication list itself needs physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: I pay 100% in advance and fly in. If the physician then decides Panchakarma is not right for me, do I get a refund, a switch to a gentler programme, or nothing?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page requires full prepayment and gives no refund within 15 days of arrival. /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ gives no refund for early departure. This is the biggest financial fear for an older international patient.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (policy). Partial: /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ allows medical-emergency exceptions with management approval, and the free pre-screen on /online-consultation/ lowers the risk.

objectionGaps.question: How many nights do I need (7, 14 or 21), and what is the realistic total cost including the procedures, medicines and tests?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page gives 7–21 days in the FAQ and 14 nights minimum elsewhere, prices per villa per night, and even lists Panchakarma as an add-on. The patient cannot budget.
objectionGaps.answerSource: This page (villa rates, 14-night minimum) and /faqs-downloads/ (Panchakarma from 14 nights). Whether the procedures are included, and an indicative cost for medicines and tests, needs physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: What is a main-procedure day really like? How long do the vomiting or purgation last, am I confined to my villa, is a nurse or doctor with me, and is there a private toilet?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The only daily routine shown is a generic wellness day (06:30 yoga, 11:00 nature walk), which cannot be true on emesis or purgation days. The unknown is what stops people booking.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner. The attached bathroom per villa is stated on /faqs-downloads/.

objectionGaps.question: What side effects might I have (weakness, dehydration, dizziness, headache), and how are they managed?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page claims "Zero adverse reactions" while /faqs-downloads/ admits mild detoxification symptoms. The contradiction destroys trust. An honest answer builds it.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ ("Will I experience any side effects during treatment?"). Procedure-specific risks and how they are managed need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: If I become seriously unwell (chest pain, severe dehydration, low blood sugar), is a doctor on campus at night, and how far is the nearest emergency hospital?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients aged 40–70 with other conditions are travelling to rural Palakkad. Emergency cover decides the booking for them and their families.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (arrangements with nearby hospitals, 24-hour assistance, emergency services on call, advice to buy evacuation insurance). Night doctor or nurse cover and the nearest hospital's name and distance need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: Who will my physician be, what are their qualifications, will the same doctor see me throughout, and do they speak my language (German, French, Russian, Arabic)?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page says "Doctor might change as subject to availability" and mentions "multilingual staff" without naming a language. Continuity and language matter most on emesis and enema days.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /online-consultation/ (Dr. Deepu John, Chief Physician & Head of Department, BAMS, 12+ years, helped draft the NABH Panchakarma Clinic Standards; Dr. Akhila Oommen and Dr. Rahul R, BAMS). Languages and continuity need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: When will I feel results and how long do they last? Will I feel worse before I feel better?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page's only answer is the unsourced "87% within two weeks / 94% long-term". Many people feel tired for days after the procedures, and a patient needs to plan work and travel around that.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (the page's statistics must not be reused)

objectionGaps.question: Do I need blood tests or reports before I come, and will you run tests on arrival? At what cost?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page says "Bring ... recent reports" and that lab tests cost extra, but not which tests or how much. Older patients often have recent bloodwork they can bring.
objectionGaps.answerSource: This page (bring reports; tests extra) and /online-consultation/ (health-summary step, reports optional). Which tests and what they cost need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: What will I eat? Will I fast, drink medicated ghee or eat only kitchari? Can you handle diabetes, gluten or lactose intolerance? With coffee banned, how do I cope with caffeine withdrawal?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Diet on procedure days differs from the "three organic, sattvic meals" described. Ghee intake worries people with high cholesterol or diabetes, and caffeine withdrawal causes headaches.
objectionGaps.answerSource: This page (vegetarian or vegan meals, coffee abstinence) and /faqs-downloads/ (dietary restrictions and allergies; caffeine-free campus). The procedure-phase diet and any internal oleation need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: How soon after my last procedure can I take a long-haul flight, and what must I avoid for the first weeks at home?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The flight home is booked before arrival. Post-procedure recovery rules decide the departure date and the length of the stay.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: What follow-up do I get once I'm home: online reviews, medicines shipped abroad, a discharge summary for my own doctor? What does it cost?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page only says "Continuous post-discharge wellness plan". Patients abroad need to know their GP will get documents and that they can get medicines.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (online follow-ups at 1, 3 and 6 months; admission and discharge notes; pharmacy supply to take home). Follow-up cost and international shipping or customs need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: Which visa do I need (e-Visa, Medical Visa, Medical Attendant Visa for my spouse), and will you send an invitation letter?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: A stay of at least 14 nights for treatment raises the question of whether a tourist e-Visa is appropriate.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (visa FAQ and invitation letter on request) and /how-to-reach/ (visa and entry, official portal link)

objectionGaps.question: Is the airport transfer included, which airport should I fly into, and can someone meet me late at night?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This page lists transfers under Inclusions, but /faqs-downloads/ charges for them. Older travellers need door-to-door certainty.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (Coimbatore 75 km, about 2 hours; transfer ₹6,775 MPV one way; book 48 hours ahead) and /how-to-reach/. The included-or-extra conflict needs physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: Can my spouse come without having Panchakarma, what do they pay, and can they follow a lighter programme?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients aged 40–70 rarely travel alone for 2–3 weeks.
objectionGaps.answerSource: This page (add-ons: extra bed ₹3,000 / €38 / $43; extra meals ₹5,500 / €69 / $79) and /faqs-downloads/ (companion FAQ; two people on different programmes)

objectionGaps.question: What happens if Panchakarma doesn't help my complaint? Is there a review, an extension or any credit?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page's promises ("permanently resolving disease") raise expectations. An honest answer about what happens if it doesn't work lowers the perceived risk.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: Is this a hospital or a spa? Will my insurer reimburse it, and will you issue admission and discharge papers?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The same page lists "Spa", "Luxury Hotel" and "Resort" awards and a "Book Your Stay" button. Insurers and employers reject holiday invoices.
objectionGaps.answerSource: This page (NABH certificate AH-2024-0250, valid to 24 April 2027), /faqs-downloads/ (no cashless cover; reimbursement documents) and /online-consultation/ ("a medical institution, not a leisure property")

objectionGaps.question: I have knee or hip arthritis. Can I safely get on and off an oily treatment table, are the floors slippery, are there steps to my villa, and is a wheelchair available?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Oil therapies plus limited mobility means a fall risk, which is a specific worry for this age group and for the "chronic joint problems" patients the page targets.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (senior-patient considerations, ramps) and /how-to-reach/ (wheelchair-accessible vehicle, caregiver). Treatment-room and villa access details need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: Will my therapist be the same gender as me, and are enemas and emesis done privately and with dignity?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This decides the booking for many Middle East patients and for many older European patients facing intimate procedures.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: What is the best season for Panchakarma, and can I cope with the monsoon or summer heat at my age?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Timing a trip of at least 14 nights around the climate and the traditional Panchakarma season.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (climate by season; monsoon traditionally best for intensive Panchakarma)

objectionGaps.question: Where do your statistics (80%, 87%, 94%, 92%, 30,000+, 100,000+) come from?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Well-read international patients distrust unsourced percentages, and unsourced numbers make the rest of the page look like marketing.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (provide the source or remove)

objectionGaps.question: Can I stay connected: Wi-Fi in my villa, mobile signal?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients aged 40–70 often still work or look after family. This page charges for internet while /faqs-downloads/ says Wi-Fi in common areas is free.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (Wi-Fi in common areas; ask about in-villa). The conflict needs physician/owner.

verifyNotes: I checked all 66 quotes against the text of prerender/panchakarma-therapy.html with tags stripped and entities decoded. 65 match word for word. The exception is #8: the snapshot has "All-Inclusive Pricing: No hidden fees!...", so a tag splits the text but a reader sees it exactly as quoted. I confirmed the cross-page claims in the other prerender files: - faqs-downloads.html has: "mild detoxification symptoms", "over two thousand years", "Panchakarma & Detoxification — from 14 nights", "Herbal medicines and formulations during your stay" listed as included, airport transfers charged extra (Coimbatore ₹6,775), "four generations", "valid 1 Oct 2026 – 30 Sep 2027", children aged 5–12 charged 50%, and "larger villas with additional space". - online-consultation.html has "We don't publish curated quotes" plus the Google reviews link and "more than 120 countries". - personalized-customized-healing-program.html repeats the Sarah M. and Dr. Rajesh P. quotes word for word. - cancellation-and-refund-policy.html says non-vegetarian food is prohibited. - Award links: the "Wellness Brand of the Year 2016" card links to the ayush-brand-of-the-year-2015 article; the "40 influential leaders" link slug reads "most-influential-leaders-under-40-by-asiaone"; the COSIDICI heading, the CONSIDICI body and the image file ...COSIDICI-National-Awards-2016 all appear on the page. - The asterisk after "applicable taxes*" has no footnote anywhere on the page. Some supporting claims do not hold in this snapshot. There is no og:title or meta description tag, and "seven to twenty-one" and "body composition" each appear only once, so they are not mirrored in JSON-LD. Those extra claims in #1, #6, #16, #18 and #25 are unverified here, but the main problem in each is real. In #11, /faqs-downloads/ repeats the same add-on rates (₹3,000 and ₹5,500), not different ones. The validity-window conflict and the tariff expiring on 31 Oct 2026 are still real. In #9, faqs-downloads.html contradicts itself: one line lists herbal medicines as included, another says "Internal herbal medicines, lab tests and specialty therapies are charged as needed". So the conflict across the site is real. Rejected: - #13: the routine already carries a disclaimer that it "is a general outline and may vary". - #17: the answer does address suitability and defers to a physician evaluation. - #41, #42, #43: the banned words sit inside third-party award or category names, which are brand names. #41's "awarded as" is common Indian English. - #50: dropping the article in a telegraphic "Bring:" list is a style choice. - #51: "Bharathanatyam" is a common Indian transliteration. - #52: "lean protein" can be plant protein, and the page says vegetarian elsewhere. - #57: "would be given" is Indian-English usage; the hyphens are style. - #58: "abstinence is adhered to" is acceptable English; the capitals are style. - #62: /faqs-downloads/ only says Wi-Fi in common areas is free and to check about in-villa internet, so "internet ... requested" is not a clear contradiction. - #64: the page does not show whether the certification exists, so I rejected it as unsure. - #65: "massage" is standard for Abhyanga and the page itself uses it; not a banned word. I kept #25 and #53 ("retreat") even though "retreat" is not a banned word. The required KTAHV register is "patient/programme", so "retreat participants" and "wellness retreat" on a hospital page (#25's sentence is also the page intro) are register drift, not only a style choice.

clinicalRisk: 'Scientifically proven symptom reduction: 87% report improvements within 14 days, 94% sustain results after 6 months'. No study is cited, the figures appear on no other page, and 'symptom' is undefined for weight.
'Safety assured: Zero adverse reactions in over 1.4M+ therapies'. This contradicts the sitewide FAQ on mild detoxification symptoms; the homepage uses 1.4M+ only as 'therapies performed'.
'Relief from obesity, diabetes, and metabolic sluggishness' and 'Improved cardiac health, energy, and sleep quality'. These are disease and cardiovascular claims.
'Holistic and gentle weight loss with no harsh side effects' and 'Sustainable weight reduction via natural and herbal remedies'. These are absolute safety and outcome claims.
'Kairali’s program enables you to achieve sustainable weight loss and a healthier life'. This is an outcome promise.
FAQ: 'Most guests feel noticeable changes—better digestion, increased energy, and weight shifts—within 1–2 weeks'. This is an outcome and time-frame claim.
Detox claims: FAQ 'eliminate toxins' and 'assessing ... toxin levels', hero 'body detox', routine 'detoxifying drink to kickstart the metabolism', and Udwarthana 'to promote detoxification'.

FAQ: 'The plan includes Panchakarma detox'. The physician must decide whether Panchakarma is part of the weight protocol and whether it suits older or comorbid patients. The page elsewhere calls it a charged add-on.
FAQ: 'Do I need to follow a strict diet? No.' The diet is prescribed, and this matters for patients with diabetes on glucose-lowering drugs.

'Who is This Program For?' lists 'Those with diabetes' and 'Desire for healthy cardiac function and lower risk factors' without any medication or contraindication guidance. The physician must define eligibility and exclusions.

Testimonials and headings: 'losing 70kg', 'overcoming depression' (a mental-health outcome), 'shed 4kg in just 7 days ... quick and healthy results', the 'OVER 100 INCHES FROM MY BODY' thumbnail, and 'Transformative Results'. These need patient consent, substantiation and an 'individual results vary' line.
'Personalized Internal Medicines: Only physician-prescribed, in-house remedies (GMP-certified) for safe, targeted care'. This is a safety claim about the medicines.

'Clinical Excellence: Led by 5th-generation Ayurvedic physicians, each treatment is reviewed for maximum safety and efficacy'. This is an efficacy claim, and the generation count conflicts with 'four generations' elsewhere.

FAQ follow-up protocol: 'monthly virtual check-in for the first 3 months, then quarterly, to ensure ... results are long-lasting' conflicts with /faqs-downloads/ '1, 3 and 6 months'. The physician must set one schedule and drop the guarantee.

FAQ: 'You can order prescribed Ayurvedic supplements and herbal formulations ... delivery to most locations worldwide'. This means continuing prescribed medicines abroad without a local doctor, and cross-border import legality is unconfirmed.
Process step 02 ('body-mind imbalances caused by stress or high work demands') is copied from a stress programme. The physician should write the actual weight-management assessment.

Missing and needs physician authorship before go-live: guidance on continuing allopathic medicines (especially insulin, sulfonylureas, GLP-1 agonists and antihypertensives), contraindications and BMI/comorbidity limits, and the realistic expected-results statement.
verifyNotes:
I checked every finding against the text of english-candidate/prerender/weight-loss-programme.html, with scripts and styles stripped. I checked cross-page and source claims against the other prerender pages and docs/rates/RATES_RECKONER.md. All 59 quotes appear on the page.

The cross-page claims hold up:
- 7: /online-consultation/ says "A reply within one working day".
- 9: /faqs-downloads/ says follow-ups are "typically scheduled at 1, 3 and 6 months".
- 17: the homepage, /faqs-downloads/, /founders-message/ and /about-us/ all say "four generations". "5th-generation" appears only on this page and four other programme pages. /online-consultation/ lists BAMS physicians.
- 28: /faqs-downloads/ describes "mild detoxification symptoms ... headaches, fatigue". The homepage uses 1.4M+ only as "therapies performed".
- 33: /faqs-downloads/ and /how-to-reach/ both quote Coimbatore Airport transfers at ₹6,775, one way.

The reckoner checks also hold up:
- 45: the reckoner validity runs "through September 30, 2026", not October 31.
- 46: the reckoner says "A 40% deposit is required".
- 47: the reckoner says "INR was not among the 25–26 files provided". ₹22,125 appears in no rates source. The USD rates match Tier 4 ($316/€277).
- 56: owner ruling D-YOGA-PRIVATE says "Do not carry 'group' to any site".
- 19: the reckoner flags whether award proper nouns are exempt from the lock as an open question.

Other confirmations:
- 8: "wellness trackers" appears on no other page.
- 25: "high work demands" is copied from the rejuvenation/detox page.
- 40: the thumbnail alt is "a woman captioned OVER 100 INCHES FROM MY BODY", attached to Rupak Mann's testimonial.
- 54: the asterisk after "taxes*" has no footnote.
- 26 and 48: the same wording appears on 30 and 31 pages, so these are template-wide.

Rejected:
- 1: the WHO statistic is accurate and deliberately leads the FAQ on 16 pages. Its relevance is an editorial choice, not a defect.
- 4: "toxin levels" is the usual rendering of ama. The site's own /faqs-downloads/ uses the same toxin wording, so I was not sure it is an overclaim.
- 13: the label is styled text-transform: uppercase, so it displays correctly as "MORE PROGRAMS". The spelling issue is already covered by 12.
- 14: the hero line is the legacy ranking meta description (it is in the DataForSEO baseline). "14–28 day" fits the 14-night minimum. Shortening the brand name and the "body detox" wording are weak points.
- 23: "NABH certified" is common Indian-English usage.
- 35: "Bharathanatyam" is a valid South Indian spelling.
- 37: "Minimum two" does not clearly contradict "two therapies per day". The sample day is labelled as a general outline.
- 38: "retreat" is not a banned word, so this is a register preference.
- 39: "Factory visits" is terse but not wrong.
- 58: Udwarthanam and Udwarthana are both valid spellings.

Partly right, kept:
- 22: the heading/body mismatch is real, but the correct name is "Organisations" (ATTOI), so the heading should not be changed to match the body.
- 42: the JSON-LD claims ("Guest testimonial", FAQPage) are not in the prerender because the helmet injects them in the browser. They are still unverified here. The visible "journey" caption is confirmed.
- 48: in standard English, "Up to 30 days before arrival" is not inverted. I kept the finding because the tiers overlap and "Up to less than 15 days" is ungrammatical.

condition: Burnout, chronic stress, fatigue and lifestyle-related imbalance: a general detoxification and rejuvenation programme labelled "Shodhanam Karma". The FAQ also invites patients with chronic headaches, digestive problems and back pain. The page gives a 7-night villa minimum (programme listing: "7 nights", from INR 150,969). Two therapies a day (Abhyangam, Shirodhara, Udvarthana, herbal steam), with yoga, meditation and a sattvic diet. Panchakarma is listed only as a paid add-on.

objectionGaps.question: I take blood-pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, thyroid, antidepressant or blood-thinning medicine. Do I keep taking it, and can your herbal medicines interact with it?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Almost every 40–70-year-old burnout or lifestyle patient is on at least one of these. The page only says "Bring: ... medications" and never says whether they will be told to stop anything. Fear of interactions is the top reason a doctor at home advises against booking.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician (Dr. Deepu John): a written interaction-screening and co-management policy. The Disclaimer page already says patients should "maintain all ongoing treatments", and that should be quoted in the FAQ.

objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician: contraindications and how therapies are modified for age and comorbidity. FAQs & Downloads confirms there is no maximum age, which can be reused.

objectionGaps.question: What does "detoxification" actually involve here: only massages and steam, or Panchakarma procedures such as purgation, enemas or drinking medicated ghee?

clinicalRisk: "87% symptom reduction within 14 days, 94% maintain improvements after 6 months" (Why Choose). An outcome statistic with no study, sample or method. It also measures at 14 days while the package minimum is 7 nights. Evidence or removal needed.

"Zero adverse reactions in 100,000+ therapies" (Why Choose). An absolute safety claim that contradicts the site's own FAQs & Downloads, which reports mild headaches, fatigue and digestive changes during detox.
"92% patient satisfaction from international guests (2024 data)" and "Trusted by 80% of guests". Survey figures with no source. The owner must supply the data, or the claims come out.
"Effective Relief from Chronic & Lifestyle Disorders" and "Relief from chronic conditions such as digestive disorders, fatigue, and metabolic imbalances". Efficacy claims for disease categories.

"Restoration of hormonal balance, reduction of inflammation, and alleviation of stress-related symptoms" and "Hormonal balance, stress reduction, and enhanced mental clarity". Physiological outcome claims.
"Strengthening of immunity and enhancement of metabolic and digestive functions". An immunity claim.

FAQ: "Can the treatment help with my chronic health conditions (like headaches, digestive problems, or back pain)? Yes. Our approach uniquely addresses..." An unconditional yes before assessment, plus a superiority claim. It conflicts with the Disclaimer page ("does not diagnose or cure medical issues").

FAQ: "Absolutely. This program is specifically designed for... burnout, sleep disruption, fatigue... address these challenges at their root." Suitability promised before assessment, and "at their root" implies cause-level resolution.

FAQ: "For optimal, lasting results, 14–21 days are recommended... improvements in as little as 7 days." A duration and outcome promise that conflicts with the 7-night minimum and with FAQs & Downloads ("Panchakarma & Detoxification — from 14 nights").
The "Shodhanam Karma" label and "deep detoxification". The physician must confirm whether this programme includes any shodhana (purification) procedures, since the page sells Panchakarma separately.
Daily "herbal steam baths" (Inclusions) given to all patients with no stated contraindications. This is a safety issue for hypertensive, cardiac and elderly patients (the target 40–70 audience).
"Ongoing support ensures long-term health" (Post Treatment) and FAQ "follow-up consultations to ensure your results last". Guarantees of lasting outcome.
"Whether you’re seeking to... prevent health complications before they start". A disease-prevention claim.

"Clinical Excellence: Led by 5th-generation Ayurvedic physicians, each treatment is reviewed for maximum safety and efficacy". A superlative safety/efficacy claim, and a generation count that contradicts "four generations" elsewhere.
"Your assigned doctor is available for unlimited consultations. Medical support is on call 24/7." A clinical service-level commitment. Night medical cover must be confirmed before it is published.
"Comprehensive Health Assessment: Tailored consultation and advanced diagnostics". The physician must say which diagnostics are meant, since lab tests are charged extra.

"Personalized Internal Medicines: Only physician-prescribed, in-house remedies (GMP-certified)" and the FAQ price range "(₹5,000–15,000)". The certification scope and the price range need confirmation.

Testimonial outcome wording: "my energy levels are now fully restored, and I feel renewed from within" under the heading "Transformative Results", plus a testimonial by "Dr. Regina Joseph". The patient's consent and genuineness need checking, and an outcome testimonial needs clinical/legal review before it stays.

proofreading.fix: One heading: 'Our Approach to Customised Care'.

proofreading.quote: Choose from 50+ therapies for multiple interconnected health conditions
proofreading.problem: Contradicts 'selected by the physician': the patient does not choose. '50+' is unverified.
proofreading.fix: 'Your physician selects from 50+ classical therapies...' (owner to confirm the count).

proofreading.quote: NABH & AYUR Diamond Certified
proofreading.problem: NABH accredits. FAQs & Downloads names Green Leaf (Kerala Tourism) and ISO instead. The issuer and name of 'AYUR Diamond' are unverified.
proofreading.fix: 'NABH-accredited (Panchakarma)'. Owner to confirm the AYUR Diamond certificate before keeping it.

proofreading.quote: Anyone preferring root-cause Ayurvedic treatments instead of symptom management
proofreading.problem: 'Instead of' can read as replacing conventional diabetes or BP management.
proofreading.fix: 'Patients who want Ayurvedic treatment alongside their existing medical care.'

proofreading.quote: Tailored therapies and lifestyle plans for chronic issues, post-COVID recovery, and total rejuvenation.
proofreading.problem: 'Total rejuvenation' is an absolute promise. The 'post-COVID era' framing is dated in 2026. The og:title adds 'India's Most Authentic Ayurvedic Treatment | 30,000+ Lives Transformed' (a superlative, with a double space and no diacritic).
proofreading.fix: 'Physician-tailored Ayurvedic treatment for chronic and multiple health conditions.' Rewrite the og:title without the superlative.

proofreading.quote: Ayurvedic lunch, focusing on a balanced meal with plenty of fresh vegetables, whole grains, and lean protein sources.
proofreading.problem: 'Lean protein' reads as meat, but the kitchen is vegetarian. The routine also shows only one therapy slot (15:30) while two a day are promised, and says 'fellow retreat participants'.
proofreading.fix: '...plant protein such as dal and legumes'. Show both therapy slots. Use 'fellow patients'.

proofreading.quote: Check-in: 12:00 noon
proofreading.problem: Hospitality register on a clinical page. 'Book Your Stay', 'massages', 'serene retreat' and 'Leisure Activities' have the same problem (not banned words, but off-register).
proofreading.fix: 'Admission: 12:00 noon / Discharge: 10:00'. Use 'therapies' instead of 'massages'.

proofreading.quote: MORE PROGRAMs
proofreading.problem: Wrong casing. The page also mixes 'Program' and 'programme' (the register requires programme), 'Udwartanam' and 'Udwarthana', and 'Bharathanatyam'.
proofreading.fix: 'More Programmes'. Use 'programme' throughout, one transliteration of Udwartanam, and 'Bharatanatyam'.

objectionGaps.question: I am 68 and have diabetes and high blood pressure. Does the '18 to 65' limit exclude me, and what extra checks apply over 65?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The core buyer is 40–70. The FAQ tells anyone over 65 the programme is not designed for them, while FAQs & Downloads says there is no maximum age. The likeliest buyer reads a 'no'.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads (no stated maximum age; senior-patient considerations). The conflict needs a ruling from physician/owner (Dr. Deepu John).

objectionGaps.question: I take metformin or insulin, two BP tablets, a statin and a blood thinner. Who decides on any change? Will the herbal medicines interact? Will my sugar and BP be checked daily?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The FAQ answer is generic, and a testimonial says someone 'discontinued three medication courses'. That is alarming for anyone on anticoagulants or insulin.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (Dr. Deepu John): monitoring protocol and frequency, herb–drug interaction policy, and who may change allopathic doses.

objectionGaps.question: Who should not book this programme? For example after a recent heart attack or stroke, with uncontrolled diabetes, heart failure, kidney disease, active cancer, recent surgery or severe osteoporosis.
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: 'Who is this for' lists conditions but gives no exclusions. People with several conditions fear being sent home or harmed.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: How many nights do I need for my combination of conditions? Is the 7-night minimum enough?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page sells a 7-night minimum but quotes results 'within 14 days'. The FAQ never states a recommended length for this programme.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads (chronic-condition programmes 7–14 nights, most 14). The individual length is set by the physician at the free online consultation.

objectionGaps.question: What total should I budget? How much do internal medicines, lab tests and Panchakarma usually add?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page says 'All-Inclusive… No hidden fees' and then says medicines and tests 'will cost extra' and 'can only be ascertained as your treatment progresses'. All of this comes with 100% advance payment.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (typical cost range for add-ons)

objectionGaps.question: Does the 'Double' rate cover two patients who are both treated, or me plus a companion who is not treated?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Couples in their 60s often travel together. The tariff shows 'per night' while FAQs & Downloads says rates are 'per person per programme'.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner. Companion extra-bed and meal rates are on FAQs & Downloads.

objectionGaps.question: Is a doctor physically on campus at night, and how far is the nearest hospital with emergency and ICU care?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Low blood sugar, BP spikes or chest pain are real risks in this age group. This page claims 'round-the-clock medical coverage', while FAQs & Downloads says 'Emergency medical services on call' and 'arrangements with nearby hospitals'.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (resident-doctor rota; name and distance of the partner hospital)

objectionGaps.question: What results can I realistically expect, by when, and what happens if it does not help?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The 87%/94% figures are unverified. Leaving early earns no refund, so the patient is paying up front for an uncertain result.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner for honest outcome wording and what is measured at admission and discharge. Cancellation & Refund Policy page for early departure (no refund for the unused portion).

objectionGaps.question: Who exactly are the physicians and what are their qualifications? Will one doctor follow me throughout? Do they speak German, French, Russian or Arabic?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page says 'Doctor might change as subject to availability' and 'multilingual staff' with no languages named. The DE/FR site is 'coming soon'.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads (BAMS-qualified physicians; the Chief Physician oversees). Languages and physician continuity need owner.

objectionGaps.question: What does admission day and a typical treatment day look like for me: which two therapies, at what times, and are tests or vitals taken on day one?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The routine is generic: one therapy slot, an 'oats' breakfast, 'retreat participants'. It does not describe hospital admission.
objectionGaps.answerSource: This page (process and routine, once fixed). The therapy mix for each condition needs physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: Will treatment make me feel worse first: dizziness, fatigue, sugar dips on the light diet, BP drops in steam or Shirodhara?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This page claims 'Zero adverse reactions', while FAQs & Downloads admits mild detox symptoms. Older patients with several conditions need this answered honestly.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads (side-effects answer). Condition-specific risks need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: As a diabetic, can the sattvic vegetarian diet be low-glycaemic, with fewer juices and rice? Is there really no coffee at all?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The routine shows juices, detox drinks, kitchari and rice. Coffee abstinence is a common deal-breaker for Europeans.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads (vegetarian; vegan, gluten-free and allergy needs met; campus is caffeine-free). The diabetic diet protocol needs physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: Which visa do I need (e-Tourist, e-Medical or AYUSH), and will you send an invitation letter?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Europeans, Russians and Gulf nationals all ask this before buying flights. The page is silent.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads (visa guidance and invitation letter on request). How To Reach (Government of India visa portal). Whether the letter supports an e-Medical/AYUSH visa needs owner.

objectionGaps.question: Which airport should I fly to, how long is the drive, is the transfer included, and can the car take a wheelchair?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This page implies transfers are included. Older travellers worry about a long drive after a long-haul flight.
objectionGaps.answerSource: How To Reach (Coimbatore; wheelchair-accessible vehicle on request) and FAQs & Downloads (transfer rates, charged extra). The two pages disagree on the Coimbatore distance (~62 km vs 75 km).

objectionGaps.question: Can my spouse stay with me without treatment, or share a villa while following a different programme, and what does that cost?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Most 55–70 patients travel with a partner. The page lists extra bed and meal prices but no companion policy.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads (companion extra bed and meals; two people sharing a villa on different programmes).

objectionGaps.question: If the doctor finds me unfit at the teleconsultation or on arrival, or I fall ill before travelling, do I lose my 100% advance payment?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Full prepayment with no refund inside 15 days is a major barrier for people whose health can change.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Cancellation & Refund Policy page (medical-emergency exceptions subject to documents and management approval). The unfit-on-arrival policy needs owner.

objectionGaps.question: Will my German, US or Gulf insurer reimburse this, and will I get an English discharge summary for my GP?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Reimbursement changes the affordability decision, and continuity with the home doctor matters with several conditions.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads (no cashless tie-ups; invoices, discharge summary and prescriptions provided).

objectionGaps.question: Is this a hospital or a holiday resort?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The awards block lists spa, luxury and resort titles, and the page uses villa tiers ('Premium luxury experience'), check-in/check-out and 'retreat participants'. Patients, their doctors and insurers may read it as tourism.
objectionGaps.answerSource: This page (NABH certificate AH-2024-0250 card) and the About Us / accreditations page. Which awards appear on clinical pages needs owner.

objectionGaps.question: I have knee arthritis and use a walking aid. Are the villas step-free, how far are treatment rooms on a 65-acre campus, is there a buggy, and can I safely get on and off the therapy table?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Arthritis is the first condition this page lists, yet mobility logistics are not covered.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads (ramps, mobility assistance). Villa-level accessibility and buggy availability need owner.

objectionGaps.question: What follow-up do I get at home: how often, is it free, and can medicines be shipped to my country?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Chronic conditions need continuity. The FAQ mentions phone or video follow-up without cost or schedule.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads (online follow-ups at 1, 3 and 6 months; medicines available to buy). Follow-up cost and international shipping and customs need owner.

objectionGaps.question: Should I book this general programme or a specific one (diabetes, arthritis, Panchakarma)?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page does not say how it differs from the condition programmes it links to. Buyers stall when they cannot tell which to pick.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Other programme pages and the Online Consultation page (free doctor consultation). A clear one-line distinction needs physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: Can women be treated by female therapists and see a female doctor if they prefer?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This is a deciding question for Middle-Eastern patients and many European women having full-body oil therapies.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: What rate applies if I come in early 2027, and which season suits my conditions?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The tariff expires on 31 Oct 2026, and long-haul patients plan 3–6 months ahead.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads (season guidance). 2027 programme rates need owner.

objectionGaps.question: Is 'post-COVID' still relevant, and what about long-COVID fatigue or breathlessness?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page leads with post-COVID but says nothing specific about it.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: Can I pay from abroad in EUR or USD, and is there an option for Russian-issued cards?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Russian patients are part of the audience, and card payments from Russia are often blocked.
objectionGaps.answerSource: FAQs & Downloads and the Cancellation & Refund Policy page (cards, wire, PayPal, Razorpay, cash in EUR/USD). The Russian-card route needs owner.

clinicalRisk: '87% symptom reduction within 14 days, 94% maintain improvements after 6 months': outcome statistics with no source. Needs audited data or removal.
'Zero adverse reactions in 100,000+ therapies': absolute safety claim that contradicts the FAQs & Downloads side-effects answer.
'92% patient satisfaction from international guests (2024 data)': needs the survey source (owner).

Testimonial 'Sarah M., Germany': 'inflammatory markers dropped 65% within 21 days, and I discontinued three medication courses'. Implies stopping medication and cites a lab result. Authenticity and consent also need checking.
Testimonial 'Dr. Rajesh P., Mumbai': 'They found issues missed by Western medicine. I am symptom-free after three weeks.' Implies full resolution and disparages conventional care.
'Why Choose' bullets: 'Relief from chronic/lifestyle disorders, improved immunity and digestion' and 'Hormonal balance, stress reduction, and enhanced mental clarity' are promised outcomes.
'targeting underlying issues, not merely symptoms' and 'root-cause Ayurvedic treatments instead of symptom management': risk that patients replace conventional diabetes or BP care.
Hero and meta: 'chronic issues, post-COVID recovery, and total rejuvenation'; og:title 'India's Most Authentic Ayurvedic Treatment | 30,000+ Lives Transformed'.
'Who is This Program For?' (arthritis, diabetes, hypertension, digestive, hormonal, post-COVID, multiple comorbidities): needs inclusion AND exclusion criteria approved by the physician.

FAQ age rule: 'adults aged 18 to 65… Children under 12 are not eligible… Adolescents aged 12 to 17 may participate in select therapies'. An eligibility rule that conflicts with FAQs & Downloads ('no stated maximum age').
FAQ on multiple conditions: 'Treatment plans are carefully tailored… to ensure safety and compatibility with existing medical care'.

FAQ on medications: 'fully considered and integrated… We coordinate with your primary healthcare providers, only making adjustments with your consent and under strict supervision'. Who may alter allopathic drugs, and does coordination with home doctors actually happen?
FAQ on supervision: 'NABH-certified Ayurvedic doctors, ensuring safety and effectiveness throughout'. Wrong accreditation wording plus a guarantee.
FAQ 24/7: 'round-the-clock medical coverage by qualified professionals, ensuring immediate response'. Emergency capability must match reality (FAQs & Downloads says 'on call').
'Led by 5th-generation Ayurvedic physicians, each treatment is reviewed for maximum safety and efficacy'.
'Modern diagnostic precision blends with ancient wisdom' and 'modern monitoring': which diagnostics actually exist on site?
'Fresh, personalized medicines from on-site GMP-certified facility'.

Process step 04 therapy list (Pizhichil, Shirodhara, Navarakizhi, Udwartanam, Lepam, Nasyam, Vasti, Panchakarma) offered to a 40–70 patient group with several conditions: suitability and contraindications need stating.
'Ongoing support ensures long-term health' and 'continued doctor support for a safe and effective journey'.
'Unlimited personalized doctor consultations for complex comorbidities': a service promise the physician must confirm.
Routine detox claims: 'detoxifying drink to kickstart the metabolism', 'herbal-infused detox water' (minor).

For the cross-page claims I checked prerender/faqs-downloads.html, route-manifest.json, the public/ahv/views JSON, long-form-award-set.json and DECISIONS.md. All 47 quotes appear on the page, apart from small differences caused by how the text was extracted. REJECTED: - 33: "Reservations will be confirmed against 100% advance payments" is correct Indian-English business usage. The capitals in the "Abstinence…" line are a style point. - 37: "Unlimited" consultations does not contradict "Daily Consultation". Daily reviews plus extra ones on request can both be true. - 38: The site says elsewhere that Kairali has its "own GMP-certified pharmacy" (Karkidaka page, online-consultation page, "in-house remedies (GMP-certified)"). Nothing shows the claim is wrong. Only the word "on-site" is unverified. - 40: This is vague marketing wording, not a specific false claim. - 45: This is an SEO suggestion, not a proofreading defect. app/(english)/_families/schema.ts deliberately emits FAQPage only on the FAQ route, because Google has restricted FAQ rich results. KEPT, with corrections to the first auditor's detail: - 8: The contradiction is real. The "space before the colon" part is false: the HTML is "All-Inclusive Pricing: No hidden…". - 28: The stray full stop in "South Asian Travel Awards 2018." is real. So are the "Brands 2017" singular/plural mismatch and "Organisations" vs "Organisation". The "( 29 more)" space is an extraction artifact; the HTML is "(29 more)". - 34: The orphan asterisk is real (there is only one "*" in the file). Taxes are stated three times. "Cancellation :" and "Child Policy :" do have the space before the colon, but "Pricing :" does not. - 39: An Ayur Diamond certificate does exist on /accreditations/ (2023). Its printed validity runs "3 years from 24.07.2023", which ended 2026-07-24, and long-form-award-set.json says "renewal unverified". So "Certified" in the present tense needs the owner to confirm it. Separately, NABH accredits rather than certifies. - 42: The og:title "…Swasthya Anukula Chikitsa India's Most Authentic Ayurvedic Treatment | 30,000+ Lives Transformed" is confirmed in route-manifest.json and the view JSON. It has a double space and no diacritic. - 25: Award proper nouns are "human judgement, flagged not counted" per DECISIONS.md. Non-proper-noun banned words still appear in the award text ("leading wellness and spa brand", "guest satisfaction"), so the owner ruling is needed. The cross-page facts are confirmed on faqs-downloads.html: - 10: transfers cost extra, ₹6,775. - 11: "There is no stated maximum age". - 14: "four generations". - 16: rates are "valid 1 Oct 2026 – 30 Sep 2027". - 17: "Rates are quoted per person per programme". - 9: packages include "Herbal medicines and formulations". - 1: side effects are described as "mild detoxification symptoms". On-page contradictions confirmed: - 115 vs 118+ years. - 30,000+ vs 100,000+ patients. - One vs two therapies a day. - "Lean protein" on a vegetarian/vegan menu. - Only one therapy slot in the daily routine. - "Udwartanam" vs "Udwarthana". - "Program" vs "programme". 44 is kept because the lock's required register names admission and discharge, and the page uses "Check-in"/"Check-out".

proofreading.fix: Use one spelling everywhere, e.g. 'Pavanamuktasana Kriya', in the About text, Process step 05, FAQ 1, FAQ 2 and the FAQPage JSON-LD.

proofreading.problem: WHO's own wording (2019 Global Report on Traditional and Complementary Medicine) is 170 Member States, not 'more than 170'. proofreading.fix: Either cite it exactly ('170 of 194 WHO Member States report use of traditional medicine', with the WHO report linked) or replace it with a programme-specific line such as 'Here are the questions patients ask before starting this programme.'

clinicalRisk: Hero subtitle, meta description, og:description and JSON-LD WebPage description: 'Heal IBS, acidity, bloating & more': a promise to heal named conditions.
Approach section: 'guarantees enduring digestive health': a guaranteed outcome.
FAQ 1 (accordion and FAQPage JSON-LD): 'Effective for issues such as bloating, acidity, and IBS': an unqualified efficacy claim.

FAQ 3: unconditional 'Yes' and 'provides substantial relief for … IBS, constipation, gas, acidity, and bloating, fostering long-term digestive wellness'. It also widens suitability from 'mild digestive disorders' to 'chronic digestive issues'.

FAQ 5: 'Our doctors suggest at least 14 days for significant improvement' and '21-day program offers enhanced detoxification and gut healing': outcome and timeframe claims attributed to the physicians.
FAQ 2: yoga practices 'support liver function': a physiological claim.

Benefits list: 'Detoxifies the digestive tract naturally', 'Promotes gut flora balance and immune health', 'Enhances nutrient absorption and metabolism', 'Supports weight management', 'Encourages emotional balance linked to gut-brain connection', 'Restores overall gut harmony for long-term wellness'.
About and Approach: 'remove toxins', 'encourages natural recovery, enhanced metabolism', 'Your gut is the key to well-being'.
Process 02: Nadi and Darshana Pariksha 'identify the root cause of your condition'. It does not mention reviewing prior investigations (endoscopy, colonoscopy, stool or H. pylori tests).

Process 04: virechanam (therapeutic purgation), matravasti and kashayavasti (medicated enemas) listed for a 40–70 audience with IBS/constipation. Suitability, dehydration risk, interaction with diuretics or antihypertensives, and whether these are routinely part of this programme need physician sign-off.

Yoga content (FAQ 1, FAQ 2, Process 05): Kapalabhati, Agnisara Kriya and Pavanamuktasana are offered while 'Who is This Program For?' explicitly invites patients with acid reflux, hyperacidity and gastritis. Yoga-therapy texts commonly caution these kriyas in peptic ulcer, hernia, hypertension, heart disease and after recent abdominal surgery. The physician must confirm the screening rule and a contraindication line.

'Who is This Program For?' lists IBS, acid reflux, gastritis and 'lifestyle-related digestive imbalances' with no exclusion or red-flag criteria (IBD, coeliac disease, GI bleeding, unexplained weight loss, new bowel change over 50) and no advice to get a conventional work-up first.
'We follow Ayurvedic principles using natural therapies and herbs to minimize side effects': implies natural means fewer side effects.
Doctor Guidance: 'continued doctor support for a safe and effective journey' and 'Ongoing support ensures long-term health': safety and outcome assurances.

Testimonials under 'Transformative Results' are Panchakarma patients ('improved digestion, better sleep') shown on this programme's page. Outcome testimonials on a clinical page need physician/compliance sign-off and must be from this programme.

Routine diet guidance ('cooked oats with fruits', 'fresh juice', 'lean protein sources', 'warm herbal bath') is a generic template, not reviewed for gut patients (e.g. reflux, IBS, FODMAP sensitivity). The physician should confirm or replace it with programme-specific guidance.

No statement anywhere on the page about continuing or adjusting existing conventional medication (PPIs, antispasmodics, laxatives, anticoagulants, antidiabetics). Any answer added must be physician-authored.
verifyNotes:
I read the visible text of english-candidate/prerender/digestive-wellness-gut-health-yoga-therapy.html and checked every quote against it. All 38 quotes are on the page; a few are split across two elements, such as "About / the Program", "Luxury Stay: / Unwind…" and "All-Inclusive Pricing / : No hidden fees!…". I kept 32 findings and rejected 6.

Checks against other sources:
- #16: 'escape' is on the extended banned list in english-candidate/language-lock-audit.json (bannedWords includes escape/escapes), so the finding stands.
- #25: faqs-downloads.html says "Additional services at extra cost include airport/railway transfers", which contradicts the Inclusions bullet.
- #26: long-form-programme-set.json gives this programme (order 5) validTo "2026-09-30". The page says October 31, 2026.
- #4: WHO's own wording, checked through a who.int-restricted search, is "170 of WHO's 194 Member States". 179 is the number of Member States that contributed to the 2019 report, not the number reporting use, so "more than 170" overstates it.
- #1: the FAQPage JSON-LD has the same 'Pawanmukhtasana' spelling.
- #9: the 'Heal IBS' string appears once in the raw HTML. I could not confirm the auditor's claim that the meta, og and JSON-LD descriptions each carry a copy, but the hero copy alone makes the finding real.

Rejected:
- #5: "14 days" vs "14 nights" is ordinary usage, not a real contradiction. The 'significant improvement' outcome claim is already covered by #6, #7 and #8.
- #18: "wellness professionals" is a register preference, not a banned or extended-list word. The suggested 'Physician-led' fix would itself state an unconfirmed fact.
- #31: "recent reports & open mind" is consistent terse list style.
- #32: the headline claim is wrong. "Perfect for individuals…" correctly modifies the subject "the … program", so it is not a dangling modifier. Only the minor 'Gut' capital is real.
- #33: "lean protein" can be vegetarian (pulses, legumes), so the problem is speculative.
- #36: "Bharathanatyam" is a common, valid Indian/Kerala spelling.

Items that need the physician or owner (marked needs physician/owner, not decided here):
- #19, #20: therapies per day
- #21: yoga format, length and frequency
- #22: whether private meditation is included
- #24: Panchakarma inclusions
- #25: transfer pricing and staff languages
- #26: rate validity date
- #28: NABH scope wording
- #6 to #10: all outcome claims, which need Dr. Deepu John's sign-off

condition: Chronic stress, burnout and anxiety, low energy, fatigue and poor sleep. The page also lists tension-related high blood pressure, post-illness recovery and mood swings. Read by its content, not its name, this is a physician-led residential treatment programme where yoga, pranayama and meditation lead. It has consultation plus Nadi/Darshana assessment, 2 Ayurvedic therapies a day (Shirodhara, Thalapotichil, Nasyam, Kizhi), herbal medicines and a daily consultation. It is not a yoga course. For the sitemap: site-tree.json already files it under Treatments & programmes > Stress, sleep & headaches, which matches the content. clinicalRisk: 'Who is This Program For?' says the programme is for 'Chronic Stress, Anxiety, or Mental Burnout', 'Sleep Disturbances and Restlessness', 'High Blood Pressure or Tension-Related Ailments', 'Post-Illness Recovery' and 'Emotional Imbalance or Mood Swings', with no contraindications. Dr. Deepu John to confirm these indications and add exclusions (e.g. uncontrolled hypertension, recent cardiac event, severe depression or suicidal risk, psychosis, pregnancy), and to define which illnesses 'Post-Illness Recovery' covers.

Yoga safety for 40–70-year-olds: the page promises 'Special Pranayama', 'selected kriyas and Mudras', and 2-hour sessions 'integrating Yoganidra, Yoga Asanas, Pranayama, Chakra Meditation and Energy-based Meditation'. The physician must sign off which kriyas and breath-retention or inversion practices are excluded for hypertension, heart disease, glaucoma, osteoporosis or joint replacement, and for patients with panic or trauma history.

The therapy set for hypertensive or anxious patients: 'Two Ayurvedic therapies per day, including herbal steam baths to restore balance', plus Shirodhara, Thalapotichil, Nasyam, Navarakizhi, Narangakizhi and Udwarthana. Steam and sweating therapies have cardiovascular contraindications. The list also differs between About, Process and the day plan. The physician must confirm the actual therapies and their contraindications.

Herbal medicines alongside existing drugs: 'Doctors prescribe Ayurvedic medications made from natural herbs according to the treatment plan.' Any FAQ added about blood-pressure drugs, SSRIs/SNRIs, benzodiazepines or sleeping pills needs signed wording: current prescriptions are not stopped or changed without the prescribing doctor, and interactions are checked. 'Pre-Program … design preparatory steps' must not imply medication changes before arrival.

FAQ 1, 'This program is intended for visitors of all skill levels, including beginners', claims everyone is suitable. The rewrite should make suitability depend on the physician's assessment, with adaptation for age and mobility. Physician sign-off needed.

Testimonials under the heading 'Transformative Results' ('improved digestion, better sleep, and renewed energy'; 'a clear mind and a lighter body') are Panchakarma outcomes shown as proof for this stress programme. That is an implied outcome claim. Replace them with consented, programme-relevant testimonials reviewed by the physician, and remove the results promise from the heading.

Detox and balance wording: 'signature herbal detox drink', 'unlimited herbal-infused detox water', 'Detoxifying Drink' (twice in the day plan) and 'herbal steam baths to restore balance'. The physician should approve these or tone them down to plain descriptions.

Any new answer on how soon sleep or energy improves, how long the effect lasts, or that 7 nights is enough for chronic stress or burnout is an outcome claim that needs sign-off. The only stated fact is FAQs & Downloads' 'Stress Relief & Mental Wellness — from 7 nights', with duration set by the physician.

Caffeine and nicotine withdrawal: guidance for stressed patients who must stop coffee and smoking on arrival ('Abstinence from Smoking, Alcohol, & Coffee is strictly adhered to') needs physician wording.

The 'Daily Consultation' and 'Daily wellness check-ins with your Ayurvedic doctor' promises conflict with 'regular check-ins' and 'regular follow-up sessions' elsewhere on the page. The physician or owner must confirm what level of physician contact this programme actually provides.

objectionGaps.question: Exactly which tests are in the "Executive Health Assessment" (blood panel, ECG, imaging, a written report), and are they in the per-night rate?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: A 50-year-old executive reads "comprehensive health check-up" as a corporate medical screening like the one at home. The page's own FAQ defines the assessment as pulse, dosha and lifestyle only, and the T&C say lab tests cost extra. That gap turns into a complaint or refund dispute.

objectionGaps.question: I take prescription drugs (blood pressure, statins, diabetes, thyroid, blood thinners, immunosuppressants). Can I keep taking them alongside the herbs you name (Ashwagandha, Guduchi, Amalaki)?

objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician. The sitewide FAQ addition "Can I continue my current (allopathic) medicines…" exists but is marked no-recorded-fact, sign-off Dr. Deepu John.

objectionGaps.question: I have an autoimmune condition, am recovering from a serious viral illness, or have a cancer history. Is an "immunity-boosting" programme safe for me, and who should not book it?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: "Boosting immunity" alarms anyone with autoimmune disease or on immunosuppressants. The page targets "people recovering from illness or viral infections" but lists no contraindications.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician. For cancer, the separate /revitalizing-and-strengthening-treatment-for-cancer-patients/ programme exists. The sitewide "Which conditions do you NOT treat?" is no-recorded-fact.

clinicalRisk: Benefit list, stated as outcomes: "Boosts immune response (Ojas) and overall vitality", "Detoxifies the body (Ama) and improves metabolic functions", "Reduces stress, anxiety, and mental fatigue", "Supports better sleep and emotional well-being", "Improves digestion and gut health (Agni)". Equating Ojas with "immune response" also needs physician wording.

Diagnostic claims: "comprehensive health check-up", "modern diagnostic insight", "comprehensive diagnostics", "extensive health evaluation", "Helps identify early signs of health imbalances". The physician must define what the assessment detects and which tests (if any) are included.
"Through pulse examination (Nadi Pariksha) and visual examination (Darshana Pariksha), we assess the dosha imbalance and identify the root cause of your condition": a root-cause diagnostic claim.

Indications in "Who is This Program For?": "Individuals with low immunity or chronic fatigue" and "People recovering from illness or viral infections". These need contraindications (autoimmune disease, immunosuppressant use, active infection, cancer) before they ship.
FAQ Q2: "immunity-boosting herbs such as Ashwagandha, Amalaki, and Guduchi". Naming specific herbs as immunity-boosting needs sign-off, plus a statement on use alongside prescription drugs.
FAQ Q2: "Our treatments emphasize detoxification (Panchakarma)". The physician must confirm whether Panchakarma is part of the 7-night protocol; the inclusions call it a paid add-on.

Process step 04: therapies listed as "corrective" (abhyangam, podikizhi, navarakizhi, shirodhara, ksheeradhara, nasyam). Confirm they are this programme's protocol and how many per day (the page says both 2/day and 1/day).
FAQ Q1 and Q3: "fortify the immune system", "revitalize the body", "profound rejuvenation and insight". FAQ Q2: "promote enduring vitality and strength".
"We follow Ayurvedic principles using natural therapies and herbs to minimize side effects": an implied safety claim.
"a tranquil, toxin-free setting" and "Our tranquil, restorative surroundings in Kerala enhance the healing effects, providing total rejuvenation for both the body and mind".
Post-treatment: "Ongoing support ensures long-term health" and "for sustained benefits". This is a durability promise.
"Rejuvenates the body with Rasayana (rejuvenation) therapies": confirm Rasayana is part of this programme's protocol.
The "Transformative Results" heading, with Panchakarma testimonials claiming "improved digestion, better sleep, and renewed energy", presented on a different programme's page.
FAQ intro statistic: "traditional medicine in use across more than 170 of its 194 member states". WHO's published figure is 170, so it needs a source or removal.

The five FAQ answers are duplicated verbatim in the FAQPage JSON-LD (view helmet in public/ahv/views/ahv-page-immunity-executive-health-{mobile,desktop}.json), so any clinical rewording must be applied in both places.

The route's language-lock-audit.json also counts it twice ("escape": 2). - **"Retreat"** is not on the English banned list. I kept #17, #18 and #47 anyway. KTAHV is clinical register only, the German list bans "retreat" as resort vocabulary, and the FAQ pass (docs/research/2026-09-23-ahv-search-brainstorm.md F16) removes it. - **#5:** D-YOGA-PRIVATE is on record at DECISIONS.md:356, and RATES_RECKONER.md:297 says "Do not carry 'group' to any site." - **Checked against docs/rates/RATES_RECKONER.md:** - #2: the reckoner gives two therapies a day; only the Preventive programme gets one. - #25: transfers are "separate from course rate". - #26: validity runs through 30 Sep 2026. - #27: 40% deposit. - #32: "INR was not among the 25–26 files provided". ₹21,567 is not in the reckoner. - **#45:** the "History" nav item points to #history, which is the "Our approach to…" section. - **#33:** the "taxes*" asterisk is the only one in the visible text, so it has no footnote. - **#14:** our own "guest satisfaction" copy appears twice, so the finding is real on that alone. The "Wellness Resort of the Year" award name still needs the owner's ruling on award names (RATES_RECKONER FLAGS line 438). - **#44:** the eyebrow is uppercased by CSS, so it shows as "MORE PROGRAMS". condition: Sleep disorders. The page covers insomnia and trouble falling asleep, broken sleep, sleep loss from stress, anxiety or overthinking, menopause-related sleep problems, jet lag, dependence on sleeping pills or sedatives, and daytime fatigue. It also lists sleep apnoea and PTSD, which is a clinical risk. Where it belongs in the sitemap, judged by what the page actually says: site-tree.json already puts it under 'Stress, sleep & headaches', next to /treatment-to-remove-stress-and-strain/, /yoga-based-stress-energy-reset-program/ and /treatment-for-sinusitis-and-migraine/. That placement is right. The page's own 'More programmes' rail is wrong: it points to Spine Care, Preventive Detox and Panchakarma. /faqs-downloads/ gives a recommended stay of 7 nights for sleep. Source files checked: prerender/sleep-restoration-therapy.html is the mobile view only and has no <head>. The FAQPage JSON-LD is in public/ahv/views/ahv-page-sleep-restoration-{desktop,mobile}.json. It has the same 5 questions as the visible FAQ, word for word, so every FAQ fix below must also be made in the JSON-LD. The desktop view text matches the mobile view.

proofreading.quote: Here are the questions guests most often ask before starting the sleep restoration programme.
proofreading.problem: The FAQ intro uses the banned word 'guests'.
proofreading.fix: Here are the questions patients most often ask before starting the Sleep Restoration programme.

proofreading.quote: The World Health Organization reports traditional medicine in use across more than 170 of its 194 member states.
proofreading.problem: The figure WHO usually cites is 170 of 194 member states, so 'more than 170' overstates it. The line also tells a sleep patient nothing about sleep.
proofreading.fix: Check it against the WHO source. Either say '170 of its 194' and cite the source, or better, open with one line on what the FAQ covers.

proofreading.quote: It functions by soothing the nervous system, harmonizing doshas (notably Vata), and rejuvenating the body’s inherent circadian rhythm.
proofreading.problem: States a physiological mechanism as fact, including the effect on the nervous system and circadian rhythm.
proofreading.fix: Put it in Ayurvedic terms ('In Ayurveda, sleep problems are often linked to aggravated Vata…') and send it to the physician for sign-off.

proofreading.quote: At Kairali, we don’t treat the symptoms with short-term fixes.
proofreading.problem: Suggests that conventional sleep medicine is a 'short-term fix'. This puts down prescribed treatment and may push patients on hypnotics to stop them.
proofreading.fix: Your physician looks at the factors behind your sleep problem, such as stress, digestion and daily routine, alongside any treatment you already receive from your own doctor.

proofreading.quote: assisting you in drifting off to sleep naturally and awakening fully revitalized.
proofreading.problem: Promises an outcome ('fully revitalized').
proofreading.fix: Drop the promise, or soften it to 'to support more natural sleep', pending physician sign-off.

proofreading.quote: Visitors frequently describe enhancements like deeper, uninterrupted sleep, decreased mental noise, fewer stressors, increased energy
proofreading.problem: 'Visitors' is the wrong register. 'Fewer stressors' makes no sense, since a therapy cannot remove outside stressors. The outcomes, including skin and digestion, are unsupported.
proofreading.fix: Patients often report… Change 'fewer stressors' to 'less stress'. The whole answer needs physician sign-off, or it should be reframed as 'what the programme aims to support'.

proofreading.quote: Over time, this treatment aids in resetting your body clock and restores you to a state of natural relaxation.
proofreading.problem: Makes a definite outcome claim ('restores you').
proofreading.fix: Drop or soften it, e.g. 'aims to support a more regular sleep–wake rhythm'. Needs physician sign-off.

proofreading.quote: Ayurvedic sleep therapy to relieve insomnia, anxiety & stress.
proofreading.problem: The hero line (also the meta description) claims to relieve anxiety, which is a psychiatric condition.
proofreading.fix: An Ayurvedic programme for people living with insomnia and stress-related sleep problems. Needs physician sign-off.

proofreading.quote: Sleep Apnea or Shallow Breathing During Sleep
proofreading.problem: Lists obstructive sleep apnoea as an indication. OSA needs a sleep-study diagnosis and usually CPAP. Offering an Ayurvedic programme for it could lead a patient to delay or drop CPAP.
proofreading.fix: Remove it from 'Who is this for'. If the physician approves, replace it with a safety note: 'If you have diagnosed or suspected sleep apnoea, keep using your CPAP and tell the physician at consultation.'

proofreading.quote: Post-Traumatic Stress or Emotional Imbalance
proofreading.problem: Offers the programme for PTSD, a psychiatric disorder, with no word about working alongside psychiatric care.
proofreading.fix: Remove it, or reword with the physician's approval (e.g. 'stress-related sleep disturbance, alongside your existing mental-health care').

proofreading.quote: Dependency on Sleep Aids or Sedatives
proofreading.problem: Offers a way off sedatives, and the Benefits list says 'Reduces Dependence on Sleep Medication'. Nothing says medication must be tapered under the prescribing doctor. Stopping benzodiazepines or Z-drugs abruptly is dangerous.
proofreading.fix: Add a physician-approved line: 'Never stop or reduce prescribed sleep medication without your prescribing doctor; our physician will work with your current treatment.'

proofreading.quote: awaken to complete wellness at Kairali’s renowned Healing Village.
proofreading.problem: Promises an outcome ('complete wellness').
proofreading.fix: Delete the clause, or end with a factual line about the physician-led programme.

proofreading.quote: We follow Ayurvedic principles using natural therapies and herbs to minimize side effects.
proofreading.problem: Implies that natural means few side effects, which is a safety claim.
proofreading.fix: Your physician selects therapies and herbal medicines for your constitution and monitors you throughout. Needs sign-off.

proofreading.quote: Ongoing support ensures long-term health and addresses any concerns or needs.
proofreading.problem: 'Ensures long-term health' is a guarantee.
proofreading.fix: Online follow-up consultations help you keep up the routine after discharge.

proofreading.quote: Treatment therapies include abhyangam, nasyam, shirodhara, takradhara, thapotichil, and sirovasti.Which will be administered as per body type
proofreading.problem: 'thapotichil' is a typo for Thalapothichil. There is no space after 'sirovasti.', and 'Which will be…' is a sentence fragment. The names are lowercase here but capitalised elsewhere, and the spelling switches between Abhyangam and Abhyanga.
