objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This is the top safety fear for neuro patients and their neurologists. FAQ 3 dodges it with "ensuring compatibility".
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (Dr. Deepu John)

objectionGaps.question: Do the herbal-mineral medicines (bhasma/rasaushadhi) contain heavy metals? Are they tested, and can I get an ingredient list to show my neurologist?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Western patients have read about heavy metals in Ayurvedic preparations. FAQ 2's "natural herbs and minerals" raises the worry instead of settling it.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner. /online-consultation/ mentions the group's WHO-GMP pharmacy, but no testing or ingredient-disclosure fact is stated.

objectionGaps.question: What result can I realistically expect, and by when: symptom relief, slower progression, or possibly nothing for a progressive disease? What happens if it does not help?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page promises "lasting results" and "transformative results" with no timeframe or honest limits. Older patients with chronic neuro disease distrust that.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner. /online-consultation/ has usable honest-limits wording ("sometimes that view is that our programmes are not appropriate").

objectionGaps.question: How many nights do I need for a neurological condition, and is 7 nights enough?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page gives only "Villas — Minimum Duration is 7 Nights". Sister pages differ: /treatment-for-paralysis/ says 14 nights minimum and 14–28 days typical. International flights make this a key planning fact.
objectionGaps.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/ says neurological chronic-condition support runs "7 to 14 nights depending on the condition"). The recommended length for this programme needs physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: I am 68 with heart disease, diabetes and high blood pressure alongside my neurological condition. Am I medically suitable, and are therapies like Shirodhara, Nasyam or Pizhichil safe for me?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Comorbidities are the norm at 40–70. Nothing on the page addresses age or co-existing conditions.
objectionGaps.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/: no stated maximum age, "Modified treatments suitable for senior patients"). Individual suitability and contraindications need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: Who will treat me (name, qualifications, neurological experience), and do they speak English, German, French, Russian or Arabic?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page says "Our specialists" and "multilingual staff" but names nobody and no languages. It even warns "Doctor might change".
objectionGaps.answerSource: another page (/online-consultation/: Chief Physician Dr. Deepu John, BAMS; /faqs-downloads/: BAMS-qualified physicians). Languages spoken and any neuro specialisation need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: I have poor balance or use a wheelchair or walker. Are the villa, bathroom and treatment rooms accessible, and how do you prevent falls on oiled treatment tables and floors?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Mobility impairment is common in this group. Oil therapies (Pizhichil, Abhyanga) are a real slip risk.
objectionGaps.answerSource: another page (/how-to-reach/: wheelchair-accessible vehicle and caregiver on request; /faqs-downloads/: ramps, mobility assistance). Villa-level accessibility and fall precautions need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: What happens if I have a seizure, a fall or stroke symptoms during my stay? Is a doctor on campus at night, and which emergency hospital is nearest and how far?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Neuro patients and their families need an emergency plan before booking a remote rural campus.
objectionGaps.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/: "arrangements with nearby hospitals and emergency services", "Emergency medical services on call"). The named hospital, distance and night cover need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: What will my treatment days actually be, meaning which of Shirodhara, Shirovasti, Nasyam, Pizhichil and Pichu, how often and for how long?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The only sample day shown is generic: Udwarthana "detox", 30–45 minute yoga, nature walks. It does not match a neuro programme or a patient with limited mobility.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: Which reports should I send before booking (MRI, nerve conduction study, neurologist letter, medication list), and will a physician review them before I pay?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients want an expert to see their records before paying 100% in advance for a long-haul trip.
objectionGaps.answerSource: another page (/online-consultation/: free pre-consultation with an optional reports form). The neuro-specific report list needs physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: Is there physiotherapy or rehabilitation exercise, or only yoga and massage-type therapies?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients coming from Western neuro care expect rehabilitation. The page mentions only yoga, meditation and oil therapies.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: What is the realistic total cost for a neuro programme once medicines, lab tests and extra therapies are added?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page says "All-Inclusive Pricing: No hidden fees!", then says medicines and tests "will cost extra" and can only be ascertained as treatment progresses. That is the classic trust-breaker.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (typical range). Villa rates on this page: ₹21,567–₹48,267 single per night.

objectionGaps.question: Can my spouse or a caregiver stay in the villa and help me, and what does it cost?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Many neuro patients cannot travel alone.
objectionGaps.answerSource: this page (Addons: extra bed ₹3,000 / $43 / €38, meals ₹5,500 / $79 / €69) and another page (/faqs-downloads/: a family member can stay; /how-to-reach/: caregiver can be arranged for the transfer)

objectionGaps.question: Is the airport transfer included, and which airport should I fly to?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This page lists "Airport transfers" under Inclusions, while another page prices them separately.
objectionGaps.answerSource: another page (/how-to-reach/: Coimbatore CJB nearest, Kochi COK alternative, named driver; /faqs-downloads/: transfer from ₹6,775 MPV one way from Coimbatore)

objectionGaps.question: Do I need a medical visa, and will you provide an invitation letter?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Required planning for patients from Europe, the Middle East, the USA and Russia. Not mentioned on this page.
objectionGaps.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/: Medical Visa or Medical Attendant Visa may be appropriate; invitation letter on request; /how-to-reach/: Government of India visa portal)

objectionGaps.question: Will my health insurance reimburse this, and what documents will I get?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: International patients over 40 usually check reimbursement first.
objectionGaps.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/: no cashless tie-ups; invoices, treatment summaries, prescriptions and admission/discharge notes provided for reimbursement)

objectionGaps.question: If the physician finds on arrival that I am not suitable, or I have to leave early because of my condition, do I lose my 100% advance?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page requires 100% advance payment and "No Refund" inside 15 days. /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ gives no refund for early departure. That is scary for someone with an unpredictable neurological condition.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (a medical-unsuitability or illness exception is not stated anywhere)

objectionGaps.question: What follow-up do I get at home, can a report go to my neurologist, and can I legally import the herbal medicines into my country?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Chronic neuro conditions need continuity. "Ongoing support" and "Continuous post-discharge wellness plan" are vague.
objectionGaps.answerSource: another page (/faqs-downloads/: online follow-ups typically at 1, 3 and 6 months; discharge notes and treatment summary for your home doctor). Medicine shipping and customs need physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: Is this a real hospital or a luxury spa holiday? The awards on the page say "Spa Resort" and "Luxury".
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: A neuro patient, or their neurologist, will dismiss a "spa" on sight. Half the page is hospitality award badges.
objectionGaps.answerSource: this page (NABH accreditation AH-2024-0250 for Panchakarma) and another page (/online-consultation/: "a medical institution, not a leisure property")

objectionGaps.question: Is the Kerala heat or monsoon a problem for my condition (e.g. heat sensitivity in MS), and when is the best time to come?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Heat intolerance is common in MS and some neuropathies, and it affects when patients book.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: Can the kitchen handle swallowing difficulty (dysphagia), diabetic needs or other restrictions alongside the prescribed Ayurvedic diet?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Dysphagia is common in Parkinson's and after a stroke. The page promises only "tailored" vegetarian or vegan meals.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: Will I have to give up coffee straight away, and what if I get withdrawal headaches?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page states "Abstinence from Smoking, Alcohol, & Coffee is strictly adhered to" with no guidance. Headaches worry neuro patients.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

clinicalRisk: FAQ 1: "Yes, Ayurvedic treatment … can help alleviate nervous disabilities". An unqualified efficacy "Yes" across all neurological conditions.
FAQ 2: "Yes … made from natural herbs and minerals, minimizing the risk of adverse effects". An unqualified safety claim; the mineral preparations are not addressed.
FAQ 3: "ensuring compatibility and safety" when combined with other medicines. A guarantee, with no instruction not to stop prescribed neuro medication.
About: "an Ayurvedic Program for Nerve Regeneration". The page claims nerve regeneration.
About: "Ayurveda … offers an effective approach to addressing these issues", said of neurological disorders.
About: neurological disorders are "often caused by imbalanced Vata dosha". A causal claim that needs the physician's framing as Ayurvedic understanding.
About: "Ayurvedic diagnostics provide accurate insights".
Approach: "Customized medications from natural herbs and minerals aim to restore balance and strengthen the nervous system", and "lasting results".
Who it's for: "natural remedies for cognitive impairments" and "long-lasting results for nervous system health". This implies dementia or cognitive-decline benefit.
Why opt: "enhance cognitive function, and strengthen the nervous system for lasting well-being" and "prioritizing safety and effectiveness by blending Ayurvedic wisdom with modern expertise".
Why opt: "Our specialists focus on nervous disability treatment". Is there a neuro-specialised physician to back this?
Benefits list stated as outcomes: "reduced symptoms of stress and anxiety", "Improved cognitive function", "Strengthened nervous system resilience, restored balance, and increased vitality".
Post Treatment: "Ongoing support ensures long-term health", and "Continuous post-discharge wellness plan". Guarantee language.

Testimonials: the "Transformative Results" heading plus the single unverified testimonial "My time at Kairali changed my life … I was physically and mentally stronger" about a "neurological disease". Needs verification, consent and outcome-claim review.

Therapy list (Shirodhara, Shirovasti, Nasyam, Pizhichil, Pichu, Abhyanga) given as treatment for neurological disorders with no indications or contraindications, e.g. in epilepsy, uncontrolled hypertension or recent stroke.

Generic day plan offered for neuro patients: Udwarthana "to promote detoxification", 30–45 minute yoga asanas, nature walks, and a "detoxifying drink to kickstart the metabolism". Suitability for patients with mobility or balance impairment and the detox or metabolism claims need sign-off.
"Personalized Diet" / "Three organic, sattvic meals": any claimed therapeutic effect of the diet on neurological conditions needs sign-off before it is expanded.

objectionGaps.question: Is it safe to take your herbal medicines and have oil therapies while I am on chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy or hormone therapy (e.g. tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors)? Will they interact with my cancer drugs?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Herb–drug interaction is the first thing an oncologist asks and the most common reason patients do not book. The page promises "herbal formulations" and "immune system strengthening" but never mentions interactions.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (Dr. Deepu John): which herbs are avoided with which drug classes and how interactions are screened

objectionGaps.question: Should I stop or delay any of my oncology treatment to come?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: FAQ 2 says the programme is not a replacement, but no answer says "never stop or delay oncology treatment". A patient deciding on a 14-night minimum stay needs that said plainly.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /disclaimer/ §6 already says patients should maintain all ongoing treatment and follow their own physicians' advice; confirm cancer-specific wording with the physician

objectionGaps.question: Do you need my oncologist's written approval, and which reports must I send before booking (latest blood counts, staging, scans, treatment summary, drug list)?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page only says "Bring: ... recent reports & open mind". Patients having chemotherapy need to know whether they will be accepted before paying 100% in advance.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (the free online consultation on /online-consultation/ may be where reports are reviewed; confirm)

objectionGaps.question: Who is NOT suitable: low blood counts, metastatic disease, recent surgery, a port/PICC line, lymphoedema, bone metastases, radiotherapy skin reactions?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: "Who is this programme for" lists only two lines and no exclusions. Massage, heat, steam baths and purgation all carry specific risks for these patients.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: When in my treatment should I come: between cycles, after the last cycle, how long after surgery or radiotherapy? Can the 14-night minimum fit between chemotherapy cycles?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page targets people "undergoing chemotherapy" but requires "Minimum Duration is 14 Nights", which usually clashes with a 2–3-week cycle.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (the 14-night minimum is on this page; timing and exceptions need the physician)

objectionGaps.question: Which therapies will I actually receive: Panchakarma purgation, Abhyanga, Shirodhara, Udwarthana, herbal steam? Are they changed for cancer patients?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The daily routine is generic, e.g. "Udwarthana ... to promote detoxification" and a warm herbal bath. Patients with neuropathy, fatigue or fragile skin need to know the therapies are adapted.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: What happens if I get a fever, infection or other complication during my stay? Which hospital with oncology or emergency care is nearest, how far is it, and is a doctor on site at night?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Neutropenic fever is a medical emergency for chemotherapy patients far from their own oncology team.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ says there are "arrangements with nearby hospitals and emergency services" and recommends evacuation insurance; the hospital name, distance and night cover need owner

objectionGaps.question: Is it safe for an immunocompromised patient to take part in group yoga, the pool, the organic farm visit and the soil/composting class?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The weekly schedule includes a farm visit and a class on "Soil health and composting". Soil and shared-water exposure is an infection risk during chemotherapy, and infection control is not mentioned.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (infection-control policy, which activities are physician-cleared)

objectionGaps.question: Does the physician have experience with cancer patients? Will they talk to my oncologist and give me notes to take home?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients aged 40–70 trust their oncologist first and need to know the Ayurvedic physician will work with them, not against them.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /online-consultation/ names Dr. Deepu John (Chief Physician, BAMS), Dr. Akhila Oommen and Dr. Rahul R; /faqs-downloads/ confirms discharge notes and treatment summaries for your home doctor; oncology experience needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: What can I realistically expect to improve (fatigue, appetite, nausea, sleep, neuropathy, mood), how soon, and how is progress measured?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page offers "Transformative Results" but no condition-specific, honest expectations. Overpromising here is both a trust risk and a clinical risk.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (no outcome may be invented; /disclaimer/ §7 already states no results are guaranteed)

objectionGaps.question: Is this price per villa or per person, what will 14 nights cost in total, and roughly how much should I budget for medicines and blood tests?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The tariff shows per-night figures without a basis. The page says "All-Inclusive" yet lists medicines, lab tests and Panchakarma as extras, which may be a large part of the cost for this condition.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs owner (rate basis and a typical medicine/lab cost range)

objectionGaps.question: If my oncologist postpones my cycle or I am too unwell to fly, do I lose my 100% advance?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Cancer schedules change often. The page requires 100% advance and gives no refund under 15 days, with nothing about medical postponement.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs owner (medical-postponement policy); the general policy is on /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ and /faqs-downloads/

objectionGaps.question: Are airport transfers included, and how far is the hospital from the airport?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This page lists airport transfers under Inclusions, but /faqs-downloads/ says they cost extra. The two pages also disagree on distance: Coimbatore is 75 km on /faqs-downloads/ and ~62 km on /how-to-reach/; Kochi is 125 km vs ~115 km.

objectionGaps.question: Which visa do I need for supportive cancer care: tourist, e-Medical, Medical Attendant for my spouse? Will you send an invitation letter?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients from Russia, the Middle East, Europe and the USA need this before booking flights, and a companion needs its own visa type.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (Medical Visa / Medical Attendant Visa, invitation letter on request) and /how-to-reach/; the current rules are on the Government of India visa portal

objectionGaps.question: Can my spouse or carer stay with me, what does it cost, and can they also have treatment?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Most patients having chemotherapy will not travel alone, and a carer's cost changes the decision.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (extra bed ₹3,000 / $43 / €38 and extra meals ₹5,500 / $79 / €69 per night); whether the carer can have treatment needs owner

objectionGaps.question: I am 68 with diabetes and heart disease as well as cancer. Can I still come?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients aged 40–70 often have comorbidities; the page says nothing about age or other conditions.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (no stated maximum age); comorbidity suitability needs physician

objectionGaps.question: Is the vegetarian sattvic diet enough if I am losing weight or have mouth sores or taste changes? Can it be made soft, high-protein or diabetic?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Nutrition is a top worry during chemotherapy. The page's "lean protein sources" line is confusing for a vegetarian kitchen.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /ayurvedic-cuisine/ and /faqs-downloads/ (organic vegetarian meals); adaptations for cancer patients need physician

objectionGaps.question: The routine starts at 06:00 with 30–45 minutes of yoga and a nature walk. Can I rest if I am exhausted, and are sessions optional?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Cancer-related fatigue is common. The page says the day plan "may vary" but does not say that rest is allowed.
objectionGaps.answerSource: partly on this page ("The above day plan is a general outline and may vary..."); the intensity policy for cancer patients needs physician

objectionGaps.question: Is the campus step-free and wheelchair-accessible (villas, therapy rooms, dining hall), and how far are the walks between buildings?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients with weakness, neuropathy or low blood counts may not manage long walks or stairs.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /how-to-reach/ (wheelchair-accessible vehicle and accompanying caregiver can be arranged); on-campus accessibility needs owner

objectionGaps.question: In which languages can I speak with the doctor? Is an interpreter available for German, French, Russian or Arabic?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Discussing cancer symptoms and medicines through a language barrier is unsafe. The page says only "multilingual staff".
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs owner (languages actually spoken by physicians and staff); /how-to-reach/ says only that English is widely spoken

objectionGaps.question: Is this a hospital or a wellness resort? Are there nurses and doctors on site every day and at night?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page shows spa awards, luxury villas, a puppet show and a pool, which makes a cancer patient or their family doubt the clinical setting.
objectionGaps.answerSource: this page (NABH certificate AH-2024-0250) and /faqs-downloads/ (NABH-accredited hospital, BAMS physicians); staffing and night cover need owner

objectionGaps.question: Can I keep taking the herbal medicines at home, will customs in my country allow them, and are they tested for heavy metals?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Liver and kidney function are often strained during chemotherapy. Product quality and legal import matter to patients from the EU, USA, Russia and the Gulf.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (in-house pharmacy, home supply, online follow-up); testing, GMP status and import legality need owner/physician

objectionGaps.question: What if I feel no benefit? Is there any refund or follow-up?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: An expensive international trip with an uncertain result needs an honest expectation set in advance.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs owner; /disclaimer/ §7 (outcomes not guaranteed) can support honest wording

objectionGaps.question: Will my health insurance pay for any of it, and what documents will I get?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: It decides affordability for many European and Gulf patients.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (invoices, treatment summaries, admission/discharge notes for reimbursement; approval depends on the insurer)

objectionGaps.question: Is emotional or psychological support available (counselling, not only meditation)?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: About says "Cancer patients’ physical and mental problems are addressed", but only group meditation and yoga are described.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs owner/physician

objectionGaps.question: Is a long-haul flight safe for me (blood-clot risk, low blood counts), and which season is best in Palakkad?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Cancer raises the risk of blood clots on long flights, and Kerala's heat from March to May may be hard on fatigued patients.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (seasonal temperatures); flight fitness is for the patient's own oncologist, to be said plainly on the page

clinicalRisk: Title, H1, meta and OG framing: "Ayurvedic Cancer Recovery & Strengthening Program" and "Boost immunity, reduce side effects & regain strength with Kairali’s Ayurvedic cancer recovery program". This implies recovery from cancer and states outcomes.
FAQ 2: "...lowering symptoms, managing side effects, and promoting a full recovery." This implies full recovery from cancer.

FAQ 1: "boosting immunity, minimizing side effects". FAQ 3: "immune system strengthening, stress reduction, energy enhancement, and detoxification". These are immunity and detox claims to cancer patients, including those on immunotherapy.
FAQ 4: treatments tailored to "cancer types". This implies cancer-type-specific protocols. The physician must confirm which cancer types and treatment stages are accepted or excluded.

About: "Cancer patients’ physical and mental problems are addressed by these treatments", "enhancing immunity, reviving vitality" and "has a long history of offering comprehensive care" for cancer patients. Efficacy and track-record claims.
Who it is for: "Patients undergoing chemotherapy for cancer". Whether residential therapy during active chemotherapy is suitable, and on what clearance, needs physician sign-off.
Process step 04: "Panchakarma, a comprehensive detoxification process, helps eliminate toxins from the body", presented as standard for these patients.

Why choose / Benefits: "By strengthening the immune system, it reduces the risk of illnesses", "It focuses on preventing health issues before they arise", "prevents potential health issues" and "supporting long-term wellness and longevity". Longevity implies survival benefit.
"Transformative Results" H2 over three generic Panchakarma testimonials on a cancer page. Implies outcomes this programme may not deliver.

Daily routine and inclusions given to chemotherapy patients without adaptation: "Udwarthana (herbal powder massage), to promote detoxification", "herbal steam baths", "a warm herbal bath", "detoxifying drink to kickstart the metabolism", 30–45 min yoga asanas, daily group yoga, nature walks. Intensity and suitability need sign-off.
Organic farm visit and the "Soil health and composting" agriculture class, offered with no infection-control note to possibly immunocompromised patients.
Sunday session: "practical do’s and don’ts to maintain optimal health and prevent diseases naturally". A disease-prevention claim.
During Treatment: "continued doctor support for a safe and effective journey". A safety and efficacy promise.
Follow-up: "The practitioner may suggest herbal supplements" and "Continuous post-discharge wellness plan". Herbal medicines continued at home alongside oncology drugs need an interaction statement.

Missing safety statement: the page never tells patients to keep their oncology treatment, or that herbs are screened against their cancer drugs. /disclaimer/ §6 has general wording; a cancer-specific version needs physician sign-off.
Classical programme name "Karkaroga Sahayam Chikitsa": the physician should confirm the correct term and spelling (Karkataroga?).

- #15, #37, #38, #39: confirmed against prerender/faqs-downloads.html. That page says airport/railway transfers are an extra cost (Coimbatore ₹6,775 / ₹23,711). It gives the extra bed and meals rates as "valid 1 Oct 2026 – 30 Sep 2027", which overlaps this page's validity ending 31 Oct 2026. It says ages 5–12 pay 50% for food and extra bedding, yet this page charges the child extra bed INR 3,000, the same as an adult. Its cancellation wording is clear where this page's is not.

REJECTED (6):

- #25: earlier briefs and reports in this repo treat "World Luxury Award Winner" as an allowed award title, and the owner's decision on it is still open as Q-08b (docs/reports/2026-09-23-ahv-search-build.md). It is not a new finding.

- #47: "Karkaroga" matches the standard Hindi term for cancer, "कर्क रोग" (kark rog), and Sanskrit karka means crab. It is a valid form, and the auditor was unsure as well.

The build deliberately emits it only on /faqs-downloads/: the comment in app/(english)/_families/schema.ts cites Google's Aug 2023 restriction on FAQ rich results. Generating it from the current answers would republish the medical overclaims. This is not a proofreading defect.

clinicalRisk: Hero, meta and og description: "Heal slip disc naturally … Restore spine health" promises healing and restoration of a structural disc lesion.
The programme name "Spinal Disc & Nerve Restoration Treatment" and the Sanskrit name "Snayu Bala Chikitsa" imply nerve repair. Physician to confirm both names are clinically accurate.

Recurrence and cure claims: "not only heals your spine comprehensively but also rejuvenates it, reducing the chances of recurrence"; "heal the slip disc, relieve pain, and prevent recurrence"; "prevent slip disc recurrence"; "Our approach ensures long-term relief, prevention".
Tissue and disc regeneration: "promote tissue regeneration" (Approach, Process step 05, FAQ 2) and "nourish spinal discs".

"a successful track record of treating 30,000+ slip disc patients" and "proven track record in slip disc treatment": unsourced patient volume and success claim. Scope and evidence are needed from the owner, or remove.

Medication and surgery-avoidance messaging: "reducing the need for pain medications" and "avoid or minimize the use of pain medications and invasive procedures". This needs physician wording plus a red-flag statement (bladder/bowel change, saddle numbness, progressive weakness or foot drop means urgent medical assessment, not this programme).

FAQ 3 safety claim "generally safe as it utilizes natural therapies and herbal medications": the physician must state contraindications and how herbal medicines are checked against existing prescriptions.
"Our ancient Ayurvedic treatments … provide stability and firmness to the affected area" and "offer a tangible solution to spine problems" are efficacy claims.

The therapy protocol differs across sections (Elakizhi/Vasti/Kativasti vs Abhyanga/Pizhichil/Kati Basti/Greeva Basti). The physician must approve one list and say whether "Vasti" (Panchakarma enema) is part of this programme.

The generic day plan includes Udwarthana (herbal powder massage) "to promote detoxification", 30–45 min yoga asanas at 06:30, daily group yoga and a nature walk. The physician must confirm suitability for acute disc or nerve pain, or state that activity is prescribed per patient.
"Ayurveda … views slip disc as a Vata dosha imbalance affecting movement and the nervous system": this traditional framing needs physician approval.
The FAQ 1 definition of a slip disc is imprecise and states symptoms as certain. Physician to approve a corrected definition.

A testimonial-based outcome claim (Mrs. Ashu: "regain the flexibility I had feared I had permanently lost") sits under the heading "Transformative Results". It needs patient consent on file, and the owner and legal must check whether outcome testimonials are permitted in Ayurvedic treatment advertising.
The promise of "Daily Consultation" with a physician (package icons) vs "Daily wellness check-ins": owner and physician to confirm what is actually delivered daily.
verifyNotes:
53 of 61 findings kept, 8 rejected: 42, 47, 48, 50, 52, 57, 58, 60. This was an audit; nothing was changed. The snapshot is the mobile view.

How each was checked:
- Quotes were matched against the decoded HTML and a tag-stripped copy of english-candidate/prerender/treatment-for-slip-disc.html.
- 59 of 61 quotes were found in the snapshot.
- Item 14 (the trust strip) is on the page twice. It only failed the first match because "118" sits in its own span.
- Item 45 is not in the snapshot, which has no <head>. It is verified in english-candidate/route-manifest.json, routes[213].metadata.ogTitle, which reads exactly "Spinal Disc & Nerve Restoration TreatmentSnayu Bala Chikitsa (…)". The same entry confirms the SEO title "…at Kairali Retreat" (item 44) and the meta/og description (item 30).
- Items 53, 54 and 55 are real. Each h2 has its highlighted word in a <mark> inside the same heading, so they read "Our Approach Spinal Disc…", "Benefits Treatment for…" and "Why Treatment for Slip Disc".

Cross-page claims checked against other snapshots:
- /faqs-downloads/ lists airport and railway transfers as "Additional services at extra cost" (21).
- It gives "valid 1 Oct 2026 – 30 Sep 2027" for the same ₹3,000 extra bed and ₹5,500 meals. This page says "valid April 1, 2025 to October 31, 2026" (22).
- It lists "Herbal medicines and formulations during your stay" as included. This page says internal medicines "will cost extra" (24).
- It says "Free Wi-Fi in common areas" (28).
- It describes the Royal Villa as "larger villas with additional space and amenities" (10).
- /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ gives a 50% refund for cancellations 15–30 days out. It also has a no-refund rule for early departure and a medical-emergency exception, both missing here (29).
- The slip-disc page has no link to any /treatment-for-*/ page. The sibling pages treatment-for-chronic-back-pain, treatment-for-cervical-spondylosis and treatment-for-spondylitis all exist in prerender/. The "Discover More" block links to Weight Management, Rejuvenation & Detox and Panchakarma instead (49). This is the item that matters most for the sitemap and page-flow work.
- The 2016 Wellness Brand card links to the ayush-brand-of-the-year-2015 URL (18). The COSIDICI heading and CONSIDICI body text are confirmed (16).

Owner-ruling context:
- Item 14: the trust strip wording, including "World Luxury Award Winner", was mandated word for word by the owner in DIRECTIVES.md D-20260916-10. It is kept as a conflict for the owner to resolve with the clinical lock, not as an agent fix. "NABH Certified Hospital" also disagrees with "NABH-accredited for Panchakarma" on the same page (27).
- Item 13: DECISIONS.md says award proper nouns such as "World Luxury Spa Awards" are a human-judgement flag. The finding correctly routes the decision to the owner, so it is kept. Items 11 and 12 are descriptive uses of locked words ("guest satisfaction", "spa brand"), not award names, so they are real violations.

Rejected:
- 42: the WHO "170 of its 194 member states" line is a deliberate FAQ intro used on 16 prerendered pages. Calling it generic or uncited is an editorial preference, not an error.
- 47: "oil bath" is a common description of Pizhichil, and Greeva Basti is already labelled "(neck treatment)".
- 48: "Factory visits" is not clearly wrong. The claim that it "may not suit a patient with disc pain" is speculation.
- 50: "slip disc or herniated disc" is a normal way to give a synonym.
- 52: this sentence is already covered by 23. What remains is spelling and "day" vs "night" style.
- 57: "Abstinence … is strictly adhered to" is grammatical.
- 58: "would be given" is standard Indian English, and the missing hyphens are trivial.
- 60: the label has CSS text-transform: uppercase, so readers see "MORE PROGRAMS". The mixed case never shows, and "programs" vs "programme" is a style call.

Physician/owner items to flag:
- Dr. Deepu John must sign off the medical rewording in 23, 30–41 and 43 before staging goes to production.
- Owner facts needed: the 30,000+ patient count and its source (34); the current tariff and its validity dates (22); what the package price covers, including medicines, Panchakarma and Vasti (24); whether transfers are included (21); the NABH certificate scope (27); the COSIDICI spelling (16); the AsiaOne list wording (17); the 2016 award URL (18); and the ATTOI organisation name (20).

condition: Osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis: joint pain, stiffness, inflammation and loss of mobility. The goal is a residential programme of 14, 21 or 28 days (minimum 14 nights) under a physician. The slug and two lines mention spondylitis, but nothing on the page covers it. The page content belongs under "Joints, back & spine", beside /treatment-for-cervical-spondylosis/, /treatment-for-chronic-back-pain/, /treatment-for-slip-disc/ and /treatment-for-spondylitis/. It is not a general spondylitis page.

clinicalRisk: FAQ 1: "Ayurvedic treatment has been proven effective in managing arthritis by reducing pain, and inflammation, and improving joint mobility." This is an absolute efficacy claim with no evidence.

FAQ 2: "Ayurvedic therapies and medications are generally safe… We prioritize the use of natural herbs to minimize side effects." This safety statement conflicts with Process step 05, which says the medicines are made from "natural herbs and minerals". The physician must confirm how mineral-containing formulations are selected and monitored.
FAQ 3: "Typically, noticeable improvements can be observed within a few weeks". An outcome timeline for OA and RA needs physician wording.

FAQ 4: "Ayurvedic treatment can be integrated with conventional medicine." This needs an explicit physician policy for DMARDs, biologics, corticosteroids, NSAIDs and anticoagulants, including a line never to stop prescribed medicines without the prescribing doctor.
Benefits: "reduces medication reliance" is effectively stop-medication advice for RA and OA patients.
Who For: "Individuals who prefer natural therapies and medications over conventional treatments" may lead RA patients to abandon DMARDs.
Who For: "treat the underlying causes of the issue rather than just the symptoms" claims root-cause resolution for degenerative and autoimmune disease.

About: "If you’re experiencing joint pain, fever, fatigue, and loss of appetite, it could be Arthritis" encourages self-diagnosis. Fever with joint pain needs urgent medical assessment (possible infection).
About: "immune system strengthening" is presented as an aim for a programme that includes rheumatoid arthritis, which is autoimmune.

About: "For Rheumatoid Arthritis, a body cleansing plan is employed along with therapies like Elakizhi, Pizhichil" is a stated treatment protocol. The physician must confirm it and say whether the cleansing is chargeable Panchakarma.

Subtitle "Sandhivātam Chikitsa… { Osteo & Rheumatoid }": in classical usage Sandhivata generally corresponds to osteoarthritis, while RA is usually described as Amavata. The physician must confirm the Sanskrit label.

Hero/meta: "Reduce joint pain, inflammation & improve mobility" and Benefits "Reduced pain, inflammation, and stiffness while enhancing joint mobility… Improved overall quality of life" state outcomes as certain.
Our Approach: "Trust in our expertise for lasting relief and improved vitality" promises a lasting outcome.

Process step 02: diagnosis by "pulse examination (Nadi Pariksha) and visual examination (Darshana Pariksha)… identify the root cause". The physician should state what lab or imaging review applies for arthritis.
Process step 05: "Ayurvedic medications made from natural herbs and minerals". Mineral content, safety testing and home-country import legality for international patients need physician confirmation.

Routine: yoga asanas for 30–45 minutes at 06:30, a nature walk, 17:00 yoga, an "herbal bath" and "Detoxifying Drink… to kickstart the metabolism". This generic day plan needs physician confirmation for arthritis patients, including heat and steam therapies in actively inflamed RA joints.

Testimonial: "left with a new lease on life… effectively reduced my inflammation… managing my osteoarthritis". A patient-outcome testimonial on a hospital page needs verification against the source video, patient consent, and an "individual results vary" line.
Sunday session: "prevent diseases naturally" is a disease-prevention claim.

FAQ intro and page-wide: any rewritten arthritis FAQ answers (medication, timelines, contraindications, eligibility for implants, comorbidities, flares) must be drafted from Dr. Deepu John's input and signed off before staging goes to production.
verifyNotes:
I checked every quote against the visible text of the snapshot, `english-candidate/prerender/treatment-for-arthritis-and-spondylitis.html`. All 59 quotes appear on the page. A few are split across elements (the 118 counter, "Why / one should go…", the H2 with a highlighted part, the testimonial name next to its stars), but they read as one line when rendered. I kept 47 findings and rejected 12. I changed nothing.

**Checked against other files**
- **Rate validity (37):** confirmed. The page says rates are valid to 31 Oct 2026. In `long-form-programme-set.json`, this programme is valid to 2026-09-30. The FAQ answer about the extra-bed charge gives "valid 1 Oct 2026 – 30 Sep 2027", and those are the same add-on prices this page shows.
- **FAQ q-18 and q-13 (35):** confirmed. q-18 says herbal medicines are included in the package. This page and q-13 say they cost extra.
- **FAQ q-13 (38):** confirmed. It says arthritis runs "from 7 to 14 nights", while this page says the minimum is 14 nights. The hero also says "days" where the tariff says "nights".
- **Sibling pages (55, 14):** confirmed. `section-nav.json` groups this page under "Joints, back & spine" with /treatment-for-cervical-spondylosis/, /treatment-for-chronic-back-pain/, /treatment-for-slip-disc/ and /treatment-for-spondylitis/. All four have prerender pages. The page's cross-links go to Weight Management, Rejuvenation and Panchakarma instead.
- **og:title (57):** confirmed in `route-manifest.json`: "…TreatmentSandhivatam Chikitsa ( … )", with no space between the two parts.
- **"Escape" (16):** it is on the banned list in `language-lock-audit.json`.
- **118 years (9):** `harmony-content-brief-pack.md` says "DON'T: say the book or village is 118 years old". This page attributes 118 years of experience to the Village.
- **"History" nav item (51):** it jumps to `id="history"`, and that section's heading is "Our Approach".
- **Image alt (58):** "…at Kairali Wellness Retreats" appears in the page source.

**Kept with caveats**
- **45:** the text is styled uppercase, so the mixed casing in "PROGRAMs" does not show on screen. I kept it only because "programme" is the required spelling.
- **52:** the quoted "Wellness Resort of the Year" is an award name. DECISIONS.md line 154 says award names are the owner's call. I kept the finding because "guest satisfaction" appears twice in ordinary descriptive text.
- **29:** "retreat" is not a banned word, but "fellow retreat participants" breaks the required patient wording.

**Rejected**
- **3:** the WHO figure is accurate. Not linking a source is an editing choice, not an error.
- **4:** "prioritize natural herbs" and "herbs and minerals" do not actually contradict each other.
- **21:** the daily routine says it is "a general outline and may vary".
- **23:** "Support: Airport transfers" sits under Practical Information next to "Bring:", which is not an inclusion either. It is ambiguous, but not clearly a contradiction.
- **24:** leaving out "an" in a short list is a style choice.
- **26:** there is no evidence in the repo either way on the organic certification.
- **27:** the routine carries a line saying the doctor may change it.

clinicalRisk: FAQ efficacy claim: "Yes, Ayurvedic treatment can be highly effective for chronic back pain... reduces inflammation, strengthens the spine, and promotes healing." Also appears in the FAQPage JSON-LD.

FAQ safety claim: an unconditional "Yes... generally safe" and "derived from natural ingredients". It says nothing about contraindications, screening, or interactions with NSAIDs, gabapentinoids, opioids or anticoagulants.
FAQ timeline claim: "some individuals may experience relief within a few sessions" and "speed up the healing process".

Process step 04: "derived from potent herbs and minerals, are chosen for their safety and effectiveness". The herbo-mineral content, quality and heavy-metal testing claims need physician confirmation.

The therapy protocol for back pain differs across sections: Abhyangam, Vasti, Elakizhi, Kativasti in About; Abhyangam, Pizhichil, Kati Basti, Nasya in Approach and Process; Udwarthana "to promote detoxification" in the routine. The physician must confirm the actual protocol, including whether Nasya and Udwarthana are indicated, and that Vasti (an enema) is not a "massage".

"to rejuvenate tissues, fortify bones, and relieve pain" and "Herbal remedies reduce inflammation, nourish tissues, and strengthen the spine" are structural and mechanistic claims about bone and spine.
"Ayurveda offers a holistic, natural, non-invasive approach that alleviates symptoms and prevents future issues" and "empowers a pain-free life" claim prevention and a pain-free outcome.
Benefits and Why-choose lists: "Effective, holistic relief", "lasting relief", "sustainable results", "Ongoing support ensures long-term health".

Suitability list: that degenerative disc disease, herniated/bulging discs, sciatica and nerve impingement are appropriate for this programme. It needs exclusion and red-flag criteria and a rule on referring to the Spinal Disc & Nerve Restoration programme.

Symptoms paragraph lists "leg discomfort, and numbness" with no red-flag advice (cauda equina signs, progressive weakness, fever, malignancy, trauma) and no statement that the programme does not replace orthopaedic or neurological evaluation.

Testimonials: "pain-free for the first time in years", "feel like I have my life back", heading "Transformative Results", 5.0 stars. Patient-outcome claims need physician sign-off, and the owner must verify the source and consent (two names on one first-person quote).

Daily routine: "Practice yoga asanas (postures) for 30-45 minutes" at 06:30, another yoga session at 17:00, and a daily nature walk. Physician to confirm this is safe or adapted for patients with acute or severe back pain.
Programme length: whether 14/21/28 nights applies to back pain and what decides the length. FAQs & Downloads says musculoskeletal programmes are 14 nights.

objectionGaps.question: My baby will be about 2–4 months old. Can I bring the baby, and who looks after the baby during my two daily therapies? Is there a cot, a nanny or baby-sitting, and time built in for feeds?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This is the single biggest blocker for this condition. The page only says under-5s stay free, and the day plan (06:00–22:00) has no room for an infant. Without an answer, a mother cannot picture herself going.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs owner (infant-care arrangements, cots, feeding breaks). The FAQs & Downloads page covers only part of it: children are welcome, under-5s are free, and some campus areas are not child-friendly.

objectionGaps.question: Which herbs, oils and medicines will I be given, and are they safe for my breastfed baby? Will you write to my paediatrician?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The FAQ answers "Absolutely" without naming anything. International mothers, and their doctors at home, will ask about substances passing into breast milk. This decides whether they book or refuse.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician (Dr. Deepu John).

objectionGaps.question: I had a caesarean, or a complicated birth: pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, heavy bleeding or anaemia, a stitched tear, diastasis recti. Am I eligible, and why do I have to wait 120 days?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Caesareans and pregnancy complications are more common in older mothers, including the 40+ IVF mothers who are a realistic audience here. The page gives the 45- and 120-day rule without saying why, or who is excluded.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician.

objectionGaps.question: I take postpartum medication: levothyroxine, iron, blood-pressure tablets, an antidepressant, insulin or metformin, the contraceptive pill. Do I continue it? Will the Ayurvedic medicines interact with it?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The only guidance on the page is "Bring: medications". Patients from Europe, the USA and Russia are usually told by their doctors not to mix herbs with prescription drugs.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician.

objectionGaps.question: I have postpartum depression or anxiety. Can I join, and what happens if I struggle emotionally during the stay? Is there a psychiatrist or a referral pathway?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page claims the programme "addresses physical, emotional, and mental well-being" and "boosts emotional well-being", but never says where its scope ends or how a mental-health crisis is handled.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician (scope, screening, referral).

objectionGaps.question: Can I book while I am still pregnant, and what happens if my due date moves or I end up needing a caesarean, which pushes the earliest admission from 45 to 120 days?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Booking requires 100% payment in advance, a date change during the stay gets no refund, and the page says nothing about moving dates before arrival. Birth dates are inherently unpredictable, so this policy discourages early booking.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs owner (date-change policy for bookings made before the birth). The Cancellation & Refund Policy page has the base rules.

objectionGaps.question: What exactly happens each day? Which named postpartum therapies, how long does each take, and how is it different from the detox day plan shown?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page names only "Sootika Charya" and a massage. The routine shown is a generic detox and weight-loss day, so the patient cannot see what makes this a postpartum programme.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician (the postpartum therapy protocol and a day plan specific to this programme).

objectionGaps.question: Will a female physician and female therapists treat me? What are their qualifications, and do any of them speak German, French, Arabic or Russian?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients from the Middle East, and many European patients, need female-only care for postpartum body treatments. The page promises "multilingual staff" but names no languages.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Partly on another site page: Online Consultation lists Dr. Deepu John, Dr. Akhila Oommen and Dr. Rahul R, all BAMS, and FAQs & Downloads explains the BAMS degree. Gender of therapists and languages spoken need owner.

objectionGaps.question: What will the whole stay cost for 14, 21, 28 or 40 days, including medicines? Are the prices valid for my dates?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page gives only per-night villa rates, which expire on 31 Oct 2026, and says medicines "will cost extra" with no range. A mother arriving 45–120 days after birth will almost certainly come after that date.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs owner (the Nov 2026+ tariff, a typical range for medicine costs, and whether lactation herbs are included).

objectionGaps.question: What results should I realistically expect, and how soon? Will my back pain, energy, weight or abdominal separation improve, and what if nothing changes?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page promises "shape", "weight management" and "balances hormones" without timelines. A mother aged 40 or over who is paying for international travel needs honest expectations and to know what happens if the programme does not help.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician (realistic outcomes). Needs owner (policy if the programme does not help).

objectionGaps.question: Is this a hospital or a holiday resort? Will my insurer, or my doctor at home, take it seriously?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The same page says "NABH" but also "World Luxury Award Winner", "Wellness Resort of the Year" and "Spa" awards, and "Luxury Stay". The mixed signals undermine clinical trust and insurance reimbursement.

objectionGaps.question: Can my husband or my mother stay with us? What do they pay, and can they have treatment too? What about my older child aged 5–12?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Mothers rarely travel alone with a newborn. The page lists extra-bed and extra-meal prices and the under-5 rule, but never frames them as the companion answer.

objectionGaps.question: Which visa do I need for a 4–6 week stay with an infant? Does the baby need its own visa? Will you send an invitation letter?

objectionGaps.answerSource: Another site page: FAQs & Downloads (Medical Visa or Medical Attendant Visa; invitation letter available on request). The rules for an infant's visa: official Indian visa portal, plus owner confirmation.

objectionGaps.question: Which airport should I fly into, how long is the drive with a baby, what does the transfer cost, and is an infant car seat provided?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page lists "Airport transfers" under inclusions but gives no distance or cost, and the site's pages disagree with each other (see answer source).
objectionGaps.answerSource: Another site page: How to Reach (Coimbatore about 62 km, 1½–2 hr). But FAQs & Downloads says 75 km; flag the mismatch to the owner. FAQs & Downloads gives the transfer cost (₹6,775 MPV, one way). Infant car seat: needs owner.

objectionGaps.question: If my baby or I fall ill during the stay, is there a paediatrician or obstetric cover? What is the nearest hospital with emergency, paediatric and NICU facilities?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Taking a young infant abroad is a safety question the parents, and grandparents aged 50–70 who are often paying, will ask first.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs owner (on-call arrangements and the nearest hospital, with distances). FAQs & Downloads mentions only "Emergency medical services on call" for senior patients.

objectionGaps.question: Is there an upper time limit after delivery? Can I come when my baby is 8–12 months old, after a second or third child, or after IVF or twins at 40+?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page gives only a minimum wait (45 or 120 days). Older or later-arriving mothers cannot tell whether it is too late for them.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician.

objectionGaps.question: Food: I am used to meat and high-protein food after birth. Can I have coffee or tea while breastfeeding? Which lactation foods do you serve?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Middle Eastern and Russian postnatal traditions rely on meat broths. The FAQ says there are "no extreme dietary restrictions", but the campus is vegetarian and coffee is banned.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Another site page: FAQs & Downloads (vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and allergy requests) and Ayurvedic Cuisine. Needs physician for the lactation diet.

objectionGaps.question: Once I am home, who follows up with me? Can I get the herbal formulations sent abroad, and will customs allow them?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page promises a "continuous post-discharge wellness plan" but no mechanism. Breastfeeding usually continues for months after discharge.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Another site page: FAQs & Downloads (online follow-ups at 1, 3 and 6 months; the in-house pharmacy prepares a take-home supply). International shipping and customs: needs owner.

objectionGaps.question: Will my insurance reimburse this? Will I get a discharge summary for my gynaecologist?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Reimbursement is uncertain for Ayurvedic postnatal care, and without documents the patient's doctor at home cannot continue her care.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Another site page: FAQs & Downloads (no cashless tie-ups; invoices, treatment summaries and admission/discharge notes are provided for claims).

objectionGaps.question: How do I pay, and what happens if a problem with the baby stops me travelling after I have paid 100%? Is there a medical-certificate exception?

objectionGaps.answerSource: Another site page for payment methods: FAQs & Downloads (cards, bank transfer, cash in INR, EUR or USD). Medical exception: needs owner.

objectionGaps.question: After a caesarean or with pelvic pain, how far will I have to walk between my villa and the treatment rooms? Are there steps? Are the paths pram-friendly?

clinicalRisk: The admission thresholds: treatment "only after 45 days following a normal delivery" and "only after 120 days post-delivery" for a caesarean. These are exact clinical cut-offs published as fact and repeated in the FAQPage JSON-LD.
"Ayurvedic treatments are generally safe and gentle for new mothers." A blanket safety claim.

Breastfeeding FAQ: "Absolutely.", "herbal supplements that support healthy lactation" and "ensuring the well-being of both you and your baby". These claim a lactation effect and guarantee the infant's safety while medicines pass into breast milk.
"aids in healing and restoring your pelvic structure, promoting healthy lactation, reducing stress, and relieving neck and backaches". Structural and lactation outcome claims.

Benefits list: "Speeds postpartum recovery, reduces fatigue, and balances hormones"; "Aids in pain relief, boosts emotional well-being, and improves sleep"; "Enhances immunity, supports weight management".
"restoring your strength, energy, and shape" and "regain your pre-pregnancy vitality". Body-shape and weight outcome claims.
"Holistic post-pregnancy care addresses physical, emotional, and mental well-being". This implies the programme treats postpartum mood disorders; it needs a scope statement and a referral pathway.
Duration: "14/21/28 days, extendable to 40 days" (About) against "two weeks to four weeks" (FAQ). The physician should confirm the real range and the 40-day option.
Naming the programme "Sutika Paricharya" and grounding it in the "Sutika Kala" regimen, while admission starts only after that period ends. The physician must define what the programme is clinically.

The day plan shown: detox drinks "to kickstart the metabolism", Udwarthana "to promote detoxification", 30–45 minutes of asanas at 06:30, and pool and gym access. Is each suitable for lactating and post-caesarean mothers?
History copy: "strengthening the uterus" and "gentle detox therapies" presented as the programme's basis.
"Personalized Herbal Formulations ... address specific post-pregnancy issues". Which formulations, and are they safe while breastfeeding?
"Ongoing support ensures long-term health". A guaranteed-outcome claim.

The testimonial under "Transformative Results" (Mrs. Ankita: "My energy level increased thanks to the food advice and herbal supplements"). The outcome claim needs review, and the patient's consent to publication needs confirming.

condition: Chronic and cosmetic skin conditions. objectionGaps.question: I take methotrexate, a biologic, ciclosporin or steroid creams for my psoriasis or eczema. Must I stop them before or during the programme, and who decides?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Many 40–70-year-olds with moderate-to-severe skin disease are on systemic immunosuppressants, and stopping them abruptly can cause a rebound flare. The page's only safety answer is 'natural and generally safe', and 'Bring: medications' sets no policy.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner. The drafted /faqs-downloads/ addition A4 (continuing allopathic medicines) is also marked no-recorded-fact.

objectionGaps.question: I also have diabetes, high blood pressure or heart disease, or I take blood thinners. Can I safely have Virechana (purgation) or Raktamokshana (bloodletting) at my age?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page names both procedures as how the programme cleanses the skin, but gives no eligibility or contraindications. Comorbidities are the norm in this age group.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner. /faqs-downloads/ addition A11 (Panchakarma with diabetes or hypertension) is no-recorded-fact.

objectionGaps.question: Will my skin get worse before it gets better? Can the detox or oil therapies trigger a flare, and what happens if they do?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Fear of a flare is the strongest skin-specific objection. The site's side-effects answer (/faqs-downloads/ q-15) mentions only headaches, fatigue and digestion, not the skin.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: What improvement can I realistically expect by the end of 14 nights, and how long does it last for a relapsing condition like psoriasis or eczema?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The minimum outlay is 14 × the per-night rate plus flights. Meanwhile the page promises 'lasting relief' and 'a clearer, healthier complexion', and its FAQ says 'a few weeks to several months'.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: Is this the right programme for me, or should I book Psoriasis & Chronic Skin Treatment instead?

objectionGaps.answerSource: another site page: /treatment-for-psoriasis/, plus the RATES_RECKONER tiers (Tier 4 vs Tier 5). The triage rule needs physician/owner.

objectionGaps.question: What exactly will be done to my skin each day: which therapies, how many, and are the Panchakarma procedures included in the price?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The 'Routine' is a generic daily schedule with one therapy slot (Abhyanga or Udwarthana). The inclusions promise two therapies a day and list Panchakarma as a paid add-on, which contradicts the 'Panchakarma-based' hero.
objectionGaps.answerSource: this page, partly (two therapies a day, generic routine). The skin-specific protocol needs physician/owner, and Panchakarma pricing needs the owner.

objectionGaps.question: What will the total bill be? How much should I budget for internal medicines, lab tests and extra therapies?

objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner. RATES_RECKONER says only 'charged as needed' and gives no indicative amount.

clinicalRisk: FAQ 'Are the therapies and medications safe?' answers with an unqualified 'Yes ... natural and generally safe' and 'to ensure the treatments are suitable'. Dr. Deepu John must rewrite it to cover drug interactions (immunosuppressants, biologics, steroids, anticoagulants), allergies and comorbidities.

'Panchakarma treatments like Raktamokshana (blood purification) and Virechana (purgation) are very good at cleansing the body and promoting healthy skin' is an efficacy claim. Confirm Raktamokshana is actually offered at KTAHV and state who is excluded (e.g. patients on anticoagulants, with anaemia, diabetes, or advanced age).

The 'Who is This Program For?' eligibility list includes 'Skin infections and fungal conditions', 'Sunburn and sun damage', 'Rosacea and redness' and 'Eczema and psoriasis'. The physician must confirm which are admitted to this 14-night inpatient programme, which go to Psoriasis & Chronic Skin Treatment, and which are declined.

Benefit and outcome promises: 'reduced inflammation and redness ... clearer, healthier complexion', 'your skin gains fortified natural defense mechanisms', 'strengthening immunity—leading to luminous, resilient skin', 'restore the natural glow, elasticity, and health of the skin'.

Durable-outcome claims for chronic relapsing diseases: 'provides lasting relief ... by addressing the root cause of skin diseases', 'aiming for long-lasting relief', 'Ongoing support ensures long-term health', 'maximizes treatment effectiveness for optimal outcomes'.
FAQ duration 'a few weeks to several months' contradicts the 14-night minimum. The physician must set the recommended length by condition and severity.
'specialized Ayurvedic doctors dedicated to skin diseases': the physician roster shows no published skin specialisation for any of the 5 BAMS physicians. Confirm by name or remove.

Testimonials 'Mr. Priyansh' (psoriasis: 'My skin improved dramatically') and 'Ms Lakshmi' (eczema: 'my skin has never looked better') are disease-outcome testimonials with 5.0 ratings. Confirm they are genuine and consented and that their use is approved. Consider an 'individual results vary' line, and have Indian AYUSH advertising rules checked for disease-outcome testimonials.
'prepare herbal medicines following Ayurvedic principles for purity and effectiveness' is a purity and effectiveness claim. Confirm the quality-testing basis (e.g. heavy metals) before publishing.

The day-plan therapy examples (Udwarthana dry herbal powder massage, herbal steam baths, oil pulling, warm herbal bath) are generic, not skin-specific. The physician should confirm they suit inflamed, broken or sensitive skin (eczema, rosacea, sunburn) or replace them with skin-appropriate examples.
How often the physician sees the patient: 'Daily Consultation' and 'Daily wellness check-ins with your Ayurvedic doctor' versus 'regular check-ins'. Confirm the actual commitment.

Mechanism framing: 'Ayurveda identifies skin ailments as dosha imbalances', 'removing toxins (Ama) ... treat the underlying causes', 'internal imbalances—often the root cause of skin issues'. These are acceptable only as traditional-theory framing in physician-approved wording, not as established biomedical cause.

All new FAQ answers this audit recommends (medication continuation, flare-ups, comorbidities, expected results and timeline, patch testing, heavy-metal testing, night cover) must be drafted or approved by Dr. Deepu John before staging goes to production (HARD GATE 7).
verifyNotes:
I checked every quote against the prerender snapshot, english-candidate/prerender/treatment-for-skin-diseases.html. The snapshot has no <head>, so I checked the head-only claims (#17, #24, #52) in public/ahv/views/ahv-page-skin-vitality-desktop.json. I kept 45 of the 56 findings and rejected 11.

Checks behind the kept findings:
- **Quotes split by markup:** #7 ("Luxury Stay"), #18 (the "Approach for Treating…" heading) and #25 ("Transparent Add-Ons") are on the page. A <strong> or <mark> tag sits inside each quote, so an exact-string search misses them.
- **#52:** the og:title "…TreatmentTvacha Navikarana…" with no space is confirmed in the view JSON head.
- **#24:** the missing full stop is also in the FAQPage JSON-LD there.
- **#27, #28, #55:** confirmed against docs/rates/RATES_RECKONER.md. The 25–26 rates run to September 30, 2026 (the page says October 31). The deposit is 40% with the balance due 30 days before admission (the page says 100% advance). The child policy is under 5 free, 5–12 at 50% for food plus extra bedding, over 12 full rate.
- **#30:** airport transfers are priced separately, both in the reckoner's transfer table and on /faqs-downloads/.
- **#26:** a contradiction on the page itself. "No hidden fees" sits next to terms and add-ons that list medicines, tests, extra treatment and laundry as extra.
- **#40:** docs/group-inputs/kairali-physician-roster.md lists 5 BAMS physicians, and none has a published skin specialisation.
- **#47:** the section-nav link "History" jumps to id="history", but that section is headed "Approach".
- **#48:** checked for the sitemap work. The "More programmes" block (Spine Care, Preventive, Panchakarma) is word-for-word the same on /treatment-for-psoriasis/. The skin page never links to the psoriasis programme. english-candidate/site-tree.json and section-nav.json group this page under "Skin & eyes" with /beauty-care-and-eye-care/ (Vision Health & Eye Rejuvenation). The reckoner puts that eye programme in Tier 2 with Respiratory and Sinus & Migraine. So grouping by slug or title is misleading here, and the finding is real.

Rejected:
- **#10 and #13:** the "World Luxury…" award names are a human-judgement call under DECISIONS.md: "Award proper nouns = human judgement, flagged not counted". The reckoner also gives "World Luxury Award/Awards" as a name used in the source PDFs.
- **#17:** not a comma splice. The part after the comma is a noun phrase, not a second clause, so the sentence is awkward but not wrong.
- **#21:** CSS text-transform:uppercase makes it render as "MORE PROGRAMS", so the broken casing isn't visible. The spelling point is already covered by #20.
- **#22:** 14 nights is the minimum stay, and the /faqs-downloads/ nights are minimums too. So "a few weeks to several months" doesn't contradict either one.
- **#29:** the INR figures aren't in the reckoner, but that doesn't make them wrong. Each one is almost exactly the Tier-4 USD rate × 70 (22,125/316, 41,159/588, 66,149/945), which suggests a real INR list.
- **#37:** I can't show which awarding body gave which 2024 award. That needs an owner check.
- **#49:** whether infective or acute conditions belong in this programme is a clinical call, and nothing shows the listing is wrong.
- **#50:** DECISIONS.md rules that 118 years is correct for 2026, and the trust strip already reads "118+". Objecting to "over" is pedantic.
- **#51:** there's no wording ruling. The NABH accreditation is for an AYUSH hospital, with a scope that includes Panchakarma, so "NABH Certified Hospital" doesn't clearly overstate the scope.
- **#54:** "daily" consultations and "regular" check-ins don't contradict each other, and the page says "daily" twice.

This was an audit only, and I changed nothing.

clinicalRisk: Hero and meta description: 'Heal facial paralysis naturally… Long-term recovery starts here.' promises healing and recovery.

'stimulate nerve regeneration and muscle rejuvenation' (Approach), 'support nerve regeneration' (process step 05) and 'Our therapies and natural remedies stimulate nerve regeneration, reduce inflammation' (Why section) claim a mechanism and an outcome.
'blood purification and brain function enhancement are addressed with special tablets, choornam, and ghee preparations' is an unsupported therapeutic claim.
'offers a reliable and effective path to recovery from facial paralysis' and 'lasting positive outcomes' guarantee efficacy.
Benefits list: 'restored facial symmetry', 'enhanced nerve function' and 'long-lasting results' promise outcomes.
FAQ 1: 'addressing the root cause… leading to long-lasting results' implies the programme is better than conventional care.

FAQ 3: 'natural and typically do not cause significant side effects' is a safety claim. It contradicts /faqs-downloads/ Q15 and ignores herb–drug interactions (Ashwagandha, Brahmi and Bala are named on the page).
FAQ 4: 'several weeks to a few months for noticeable improvement' states a recovery timeframe, and it conflicts with the 14/21/28-day programme.
Programme length '14/21/28 days' is presented as the treatment course, but the rates source states only a 14-night minimum.

The 'Who is This Program For?' list includes stroke-induced palsy, parotid gland disorders, postoperative palsy and traumatic nerve injury, with no exclusion or referral criteria. For example, parotid tumours and progressive or unexplained palsy need investigation first, and a patient in the acute stroke window needs a neurologist first.

The page has no red-flag or referral statement: sudden facial weakness can be a stroke and needs emergency care, and Ayurvedic care should not replace or delay standard early treatment of Bell's palsy. Dr. Deepu John must approve the wording.
Eye protection during Nasyam, Shirodhara, Ksheeradhoomam and oil therapies for incomplete eye closure is not addressed.

Cause, dosha and symptom statements need correction: 'nerve occlusion', 'imbalances in the Vata and Pitta doshas' vs 'aggravated Vata', and 'numbness… speech difficulties' and 'reduce facial swelling'.
'Medicinal herbs such as Ashwagandha, Brahmi, and Bala, along with Rasayanas, strengthen the nervous system' is an efficacy claim for named herbs.
'Our experienced doctors specialize in neurology' is a qualification claim the roster does not support (BAMS only). The same sentence is on /treatment-for-paralysis/.
The testimonial outcome claim ('my facial movement improved… restoration of face muscle control') needs the patient's provenance and consent confirmed, plus a physician-approved results-vary note.
The generic day plan (Udwarthana, 'detoxifying drink', 'promote detoxification') shown on a facial-paralysis page needs the physician to confirm what is actually prescribed for this condition.
verifyNotes:
I checked every quote against the extracted text and aria/alt attributes of sites/ayurvedichealingvillage.com/english-candidate/prerender/treatment-for-facial-paralysis.html. All 52 quotes appear on the page. I kept 44 findings and rejected 8.

Checks against other sources:
- #5: route-manifest.json line 3972 has ogTitle "Facial Paralysis & Nerve Rehabilitation TherapyArdita Chikitsa (...)", with the two strings run together. The prerender has no ld+json block.
- #7: The facial paralysis minimum in docs/rates/RATES_RECKONER.md is 14 Nights (line 244). No rate source gives 21 or 28 nights for this programme, and the page's sentence is also missing "The".
- #37–39 and #46: The reckoner's treatment T&C require a 40% deposit, not 100% advance. The rates run to September 30, 2026, not October 31. The cancellation wording is 30+/15–30/<15 days. The child policy has three age bands, and the page gives only the under-5 band.
- #41: In faq-content-2026.json the Coimbatore transfer costs ₹6,775, and addition #22 on languages is marked no-recorded-fact.
- #2: In the same file, q-15 lists headaches, fatigue and digestive changes as possible effects.
- #16: docs/group-inputs/kairali-physician-roster.md line 91 records BAMS only ("No MD/MS/PhD is claimed anywhere"). Dr. Deepu John's listed expertise is neuromuscular disorders. The neurology sentence also appears on treatment-for-paralysis.html.
- #45: DECISIONS.md D-YOGA-PRIVATE and reckoner line 297 say not to carry "group" yoga to any site.
- #30: I found no ruling that exempts award proper names from the lock. The award text calls the hospital "India's Leading Spa Resort". The owner still needs to rule on award names.
- #50: site-tree.json puts Addiction Recovery & Behavioral Health Therapy under "Nerves, paralysis & recovery". The page's related programmes are Spine Care, Preventive Detox and Panchakarma, but the two neuro pages (/treatment-for-paralysis/, /treatment-for-nervous-disability/) exist and are not linked. This bears directly on the sitemap-flow request.
- #51: The Ms. Anita testimonial has no source or consent record in the repo. It appears only in the view JSONs and in the prerender.

Rejected:
- #3: The page does describe post-discharge care ("Continuous post-discharge wellness plan" and the Post Treatment follow-ups). "Several weeks to months" is a cautious, hedged statement, not a contradiction.
- #9: "Vata and Pitta" and "treat aggravated Vata" are not a hard contradiction. Which doshas to name is the physician's call.
- #10: "Nerve occlusion" is odd wording, but the causes list is non-exhaustive. Deciding which symptoms and causes are accurate is clinical judgement, and I was unsure.
- #33: "retreat" is not a banned word, and the project's own banned list in language-lock-audit.json leaves it out. This is register preference, not a lock breach.
- #34: "doctor" is not banned. The sitewide CTAs use "Doctor", so this is style preference.
- #43: The day plan is already labelled "a general outline and may vary based on the specific treatment program".
- #44: "Once a Week" matches the schedule, where each activity runs once weekly (farm on Monday, cooking on Wednesday). It is not a contradiction.
- #48: "Sirovasti" is an accepted transliteration.

Medical wording in kept items #1, #2, #6, #8, #11, #12, #17 and #18 needs Dr. Deepu John's sign-off. Price, policy and award items (#7, #30, #37, #38, #40, #41, #46, #51) need owner confirmation.

condition: Paralysis (Pakshāghāta Chikitsa). The page's "Who is this for" list: stroke-induced paralysis, Bell's palsy, traumatic nerve injury, nerve compression, postoperative paralysis, neuritis, muscle weakness/atrophy. objectionGaps.question: My stroke (or injury or surgery) was X months ago. How soon afterwards is it safe to fly to India and start this programme, and who decides whether I'm ready?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This is the first safety question every stroke survivor and their family asks. The page has no timing guidance and no contraindications. It lists 'Stroke-induced paralysis' with no acute-phase caveat.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner (Dr. Deepu John). The route to a case-by-case answer already exists: the free pre-programme teleconsultation on this page and /online-consultation/

objectionGaps.question: I take blood thinners, blood-pressure, diabetes and cholesterol medicines. Will the herbal medicines, purging (Virechana) or steam interact with them? Do I have to stop anything?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: After a stroke, most patients take anticoagulants or antiplatelets and antihypertensives. Herb interactions, and fluid loss from purging, are real fears for a 60–70-year-old. The page says nothing.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /online-consultation/ already says 'continue any care and medication advised by your treating physician; never stop a prescribed medicine without their guidance'. The specific interaction and Virechana-safety answer needs physician

objectionGaps.question: I have little or no feeling in my weak arm and leg. How do you stop hot Kizhi boluses, Pizhichil oil or steam from burning skin I can't feel, and how do you protect a weak or subluxed shoulder during massage?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This fear is specific to paralysis: numb limbs, hot therapies, and a fragile hemiplegic shoulder. The page promotes exactly these therapies with no mention of safeguards.
objectionGaps.answerSource: needs physician/owner

objectionGaps.question: I use a wheelchair or can't transfer, dress or use the toilet alone. Do nurses help day and night, or must a family member do it?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This decides whether the patient can come at all and whether a carer must travel. The page doesn't mention nursing or help with daily living.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Partial: /faqs-downloads/ ('24-hour assistance', 'ramps and support structures', 'accessible environment'); /how-to-reach/ (wheelchair-accessible vehicle, caregiver can be arranged); the homepage lists assistant nurses; /personalized-customized-healing-program/ claims round-the-clock medical coverage. The actual nursing and daily-living care scope needs owner

objectionGaps.question: Is there a qualified physiotherapist on staff? How much physiotherapy do I get each day, and is it in the price?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Stroke patients know rehabilitation depends on physiotherapy. The page mentions 'Gentle physiotherapy exercises' and 'modern techniques', but the package tiles list only 'Daily Group Yoga Sessions'. No page on the site names a physiotherapist.
