clinicalRisk: 'Our experienced doctors specialize in neurology': credential claim. The site's stated credentials are BAMS (Dr. Deepu John, Chief Physician; Dr. Akhila Oommen).
'Our therapies and natural remedies stimulate nerve regeneration, reduce inflammation, and promote recovery': mechanism and outcome claim.
'Specific herbal formulations and Rasayana therapies are used to regenerate nerve tissues': tissue-regeneration claim.
'Ayurveda addresses the root cause of paralysis for lasting results': root-cause and permanence claim (for stroke the cause is vascular).
Benefits list: 'Improved muscle strength and control, enhanced nerve function', 'restored symmetry', 'long-lasting results': outcome promises.
'Shirodhara … improves neurological function': outcome claim.
Hero, meta description and og:description: 'Improve mobility & nerve function with holistic healing', plus the programme name 'Paralysis Recovery …': implied outcome.

Testimonial 'My limbs’ strength and sensibility were restored', headed 'Transformative Results' and 'Success Stories': outcome claim through a single, first-name-only testimonial. Needs verification, consent and a results-vary statement.

FAQ 1 labels Abhyangam, Pizhichil and Kizhi as 'Panchakarma treatments', and says they 'enhance muscle strength, nerve function, and overall mobility': wrong classification and outcome claim. The same text is emitted in the FAQPage JSON-LD.

Process step 02 prescribes Virechana (purging) and Swedana, and calls it 'essential for recovery': purging in elderly post-stroke patients on antihypertensives or diuretics is a safety matter the physician must approve. Swedana is misclassified as Panchakarma. Basti/Nasya are not mentioned; the physician should confirm the actual protocol.
FAQ 2: 'Paralysis, according to Ayurveda, is caused by an imbalance in Vata dosha': causal wording should be framed by the physician as Ayurvedic classification, not medical causation.
FAQ 3: 'typically 14 to 28 days or more' and 'promote maximum recovery and long-term benefits': duration and outcome claim.
Process step 06: diet 'focused on boosting nerve health and immunity' and 'prevent further complications': prevention claim that stroke patients will read as preventing recurrence.

'Who is This Program For?' eligibility list (Bell's palsy, nerve compression, postoperative paralysis, traumatic nerve injury), with no contraindications or timing after an acute stroke: the physician must set inclusion/exclusion criteria and say when after a stroke admission is appropriate.

'Yoga and Physiotherapy … Gentle physiotherapy exercises' and 'combining ancient Ayurvedic therapies with modern techniques': the physician/owner must confirm physiotherapy is actually delivered and by whom.
Generic Dinacharya timetable on a paralysis page (yoga asanas 30–45 min, nature walk, oil pulling, Udwarthana): the physician should confirm or replace it for hemiplegic patients.

Safety content that is missing but needed on this page: burn risk from hot Kizhi/Pizhichil/steam on limbs with sensory loss, handling of the hemiplegic shoulder, fall risk after oil therapies, and herb interactions with anticoagulants. Any answer written for these needs Dr. Deepu John's sign-off.

clinicalRisk: Hero promise that the programme 'Includes Greeva Vasti, Abhyangam', which reads as if every patient will get Greeva Vasti. Therapies are prescribed individually, and Greeva Vasti does not appear in the tariff Inclusions.
'...therapies like Greeva vasti (neck therapy) and rejuvenating massages like Abhyangam to alleviate pain and restore mobility' is an outcome claim ('restore mobility').
'we aim to reduce inflammation, relieve pain, and improve spinal flexibility' claims a therapeutic mechanism and outcome.
'reduce stress, which can exacerbate cervical spondylosis' is a causal medical claim.
'this degenerative spinal condition, which is caused by the wear and tear of the cervical discs' is a statement of cause that needs clinical accuracy review.
'Treatment is based on balancing the Vata dosha, which is associated with joint degeneration and pain in Ayurveda' is clinical framing that needs physician approval.

The Sanskrit name 'Manyastambha Chikitsa' is presented as the classical match for cervical spondylosis. The physician should confirm the nomenclature; Greeva Graha or Greevastambha are the alternatives.
The programme name uses 'Rehabilitation', which implies a structured rehabilitation or physiotherapy component that the page never describes.

'Kairali has developed an effective and comprehensive treatment plan that includes Panchakarma detoxification' claims efficacy and says Panchakarma is included, which conflicts with the paid add-on listing.
'Kairali has helped numerous individuals alleviate the symptoms of cervical spondylosis, promoting long-term relief' is an outcome claim with no data.
'natural, non-invasive treatments' implies a safety profile.
'Those interested in curing Cervical' is an implied cure claim and a locked word.

Benefits and 'Why opt' copy: 'By strengthening the immune system, it reduces the risk of illnesses', 'enhances vitality, energy, and immune strength', 'prevents potential health issues', 'longevity'. These are general health claims that are not relevant to this condition.
'Ongoing support ensures long-term health' is a guaranteed-outcome wording.

The generic daily routine prescribes 30–45 minutes of yoga asanas at 06:30 plus yoga at 17:00, and names Udwarthana as the example therapy. The physician must confirm that this routine is safe and applicable for cervical spondylosis patients, including how yoga is adapted for the neck.
'Detoxifying Drink ... to kickstart the metabolism' and 'promote detoxification' are physiological claims.

Testimonial under 'Transformative Results' ('I can freely move my neck. My life has been genuinely rejuvenated by Kairali.', attributed only to 'Mr. George ★★★★★ 5.0'). Its provenance and consent need verifying (HARD GATE 6: no unverified reviews presented as genuine), and the outcome heading needs clinical sign-off.

The page has no statement of red flags or contraindications (arm weakness, myelopathy signs, recent trauma) and no statement on continuing current medicines. Any FAQ answer written for these gaps is clinical content that needs Dr. Deepu John's sign-off before staging goes to production.

The 'Who is this for' list covers 'Spondylitis' and 'Shoulder Pain'. The physician should define the clinical scope of this page against /treatment-for-spondylitis/, /treatment-for-chronic-back-pain/ and /treatment-for-slip-disc/.
verifyNotes:
I checked all 44 findings. 36 are real and 8 are rejected. Nothing was changed.

**How I checked:** I stripped the snapshot to plain text and matched each quote with its whitespace normalised. Where the snapshot splits a line across a label and its text (for example "Daily Rejuvenation:" and "Luxury Stay:"), I read the rendered text instead. For the claims about other pages, I read the snapshots of /faqs-downloads/, /how-to-reach/, /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ and /treatment-for-spondylitis/, plus long-form-programme-set.json and DECISIONS.md.

**Kept, with the evidence for the less obvious ones:**
- **#6:** The snapshot has no `<head>`, so this string is not in it. It is at route-manifest.json routes[203].metadata.ogTitle. app/(english)/_families/metadata.ts publishes that field as the og:title and the twitter title, so the fault is on the live page.
- **#5:** The alt text "Ayurvedic Doctor Consultation for Cervical Spondylitis" is confirmed.
- **#10:** The heading renders as "<mark>Why</mark> one should opt for this therapy?".
- **#18:** /faqs-downloads/ says "Most programmes include two Ayurvedic therapies a day". The page itself also says "Daily 2 Therapies Per Person".
- **#23:** /faqs-downloads/ gives Coimbatore Airport transfers at ₹6,775 one way, so transfers cost extra. /how-to-reach/ says "our team communicates in English". The word "multilingual" appears nowhere else on the site.
- **#24:** /faqs-downloads/ gives rates "valid 1 Oct 2026 – 30 Sep 2027". Most entries in long-form-programme-set.json have validTo 2026-09-30. The page says October 31, 2026.
- **#26:** The policy page says a 15–30 day cancellation gets a 50% refund.
- **#38:** The aria-label containing "reclining guest’s neck" is confirmed.
- **#41:** The same page spells it "World Luxury Spa Awards 2023", so "Worlds" is a typo.
- **#42:** The card title says COSIDICI and the body says CONSIDICI. The correct spelling needs an owner check against the award document.
- **#14:** Kept because "effective" is a claim about results with no evidence behind it.

**Rejected:**
- **#0:** The page has no FAQ section and no ld+json, which is true. But this asks for new content, not a proofreading fix. Its claim that "none" of a patient's pre-booking questions are answered is also overstated: the page covers price, cancellation, check-in and what to bring.
- **#9:** The Process step names therapies with "such as", so they are examples, not a contradiction. The real template problem is already covered by #8.
- **#22:** The History section describes the clinical plan and the Inclusions list describes billing. That is ambiguous, not a clear contradiction.
- **#27:** "Abstinence ... is strictly adhered to" is understandable usage; the objection is style.
- **#28:** Dropping the article in a short "Bring:" list is normal, and the point about which reports to bring is a suggestion, not an error.
- **#39 and #40:** These are award names. DECISIONS.md line 154 says award names "= human judgement, flagged not counted", and the trust strip wording was set by the owner. They stay as owner-ruling items, not errors.
- **#43:** "between the Age of 5 to 12" is common Indian-English usage.

**Missed by the first auditor:**
- **Banned word:** The South Asian Travel Awards 2018 card says "Celebrated as a leading wellness and spa brand". This is ordinary copy, not an award name, so it is a real use of a banned word.
- **Stray full stop:** The card title reads "South Asian Travel Awards 2018." with a full stop at the end.
- **Needs physician/owner:**
  - The number of therapies per day (one or two).
  - Whether Panchakarma is included in the package price.
  - The current tariff validity dates.
  - Which clinical reports a neck patient should bring.

objectionGaps.whyItMatters: A patient with a rheumatologist's AS diagnosis reads a definition of degeneration and a 'spondylosis' package, then finds /treatment-for-cervical-spondylosis/, /treatment-for-arthritis-and-spondylitis/, /treatment-for-chronic-back-pain/ and /treatment-for-slip-disc/ covering similar ground. clinicalRisk: 'Get lasting relief from Spondylitis with Ayurvedic spine therapy.' promises a durable result. It appears as the hero line, the meta description, the og:description and the JSON-LD WebPage description.
'to reduce pain, improve mobility, and provide lasting relief from Spondylitis' (About) is another outcome promise, and it credits 'expert therapists' with choosing treatment.

The definition of the condition mixes up spondylitis and spondylosis and names causes ('ageing, poor posture, lifestyle issues, or degeneration, with nerve compression and an increase in Vata dosha being key contributors'). It needs a physician rewrite that states which condition the programme treats.
'Your Ayurvedic treatment package for spondylosis': the indication named in the package heading doesn't match the page's condition.

Which therapies the spondylitis protocol actually uses: About (Snehan, Kati Vasti, Abhyangam, Shirodhara, Nasyam), FAQ 1 (Abhyangam, Kativasthi, Pizhichil, Elakizhi) and the routine (Abhyanga, Udwarthana) disagree.
FAQ 1 and its FAQPage JSON-LD: 'These therapies aid in strengthening the spine and related muscles, lowering inflammation, and increasing mobility', framed as 'spine therapy for posture correction'.
FAQ 3 and its JSON-LD: 'In order to provide long-term comfort, this also involves yoga poses, stretches, and herbal supplements' (an outcome promise plus unspecified medicines).

'By strengthening the immune system, it reduces the risk of illnesses and boosts the body’s defence mechanisms' is a general immunity claim and clinically questionable for autoimmune ankylosing spondylitis. The same text is on /treatment-for-cervical-spondylosis/.

The Benefits and 'Why opt' bullets: 'Natural rejuvenation enhances vitality, energy, and immune strength', 'supporting long-term wellness and longevity', 'focuses on preventing health issues before they arise'. These are generic claims with no spine evidence.
History: 'addresses the root causes of potential health issues', 'promoting detoxification through Panchakarma and using specialized herbs to nourish tissues', 'stimulate healing'.
'continued doctor support for a safe and effective journey' is an unqualified safety and efficacy claim.

Testimonial block: the headings 'Transformative Results' and 'Living Pain-Free: Inspiring Spondylitis Transformations', plus the testimonial's 'conventional therapies weren’t helping' (a comparison with conventional care). Also confirm that the 'Mr. Shashank' review is authentic and that the patient consented to its use.

Daily yoga: 30–45 minutes of asanas at 06:30, yoga again at 17:00 and 'Daily Group Yoga Sessions', offered to spondylitis patients with no statement that it is modified or physician-cleared (a safety risk for a fused spine, flares or osteoporosis).
Detox claims in the routine: Udwarthana 'to promote detoxification', and a 'detoxifying drink to kickstart the metabolism'.
Who the programme is for: 'Relief from Shoulder Pain' and the generic 'Relief from Pain' widen the indication beyond spondylitis.
Post Treatment: 'Ongoing support ensures long-term health' is an outcome promise.

Any new FAQ answer on continuing or stopping biologics or NSAIDs, contraindications, time to results, age limits or other conditions must be written or approved by Dr. Deepu John before staging goes to production. The agent must not draft these facts.

objectionGaps.question: I am on methotrexate, a biologic (adalimumab, secukinumab etc.), cyclosporine, acitretin or strong steroid creams. Do I have to stop them, and can your herbal medicines interact with them?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This is the first question from most moderate-to-severe psoriasis patients over 40. Stopping systemic drugs or steroids suddenly can trigger a rebound flare. Without an answer they will not book, or their dermatologist will advise against it.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician. General principle already on /online-consultation/ ('never stop a prescribed medicine without their guidance') and /disclaimer/ ('maintain all ongoing treatments'). A psoriasis-specific answer needs Dr. Deepu John.

objectionGaps.question: Which types and severities of psoriasis do you accept (plaque, scalp, nail, guttate, pustular, erythrodermic, psoriatic arthritis), and when would you say no?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients with extensive or unstable disease need to know they won't be turned away on arrival. Unsuitable patients should be screened out before they fly.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician. The page's 'Who is This Program For?' list is generic and has no exclusions.

objectionGaps.question: What exactly will be done to my skin? Which Panchakarma procedures (Virechana, Vamana, Raktamokshana/leech therapy?), how intense are they, and are they uncomfortable?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Western patients are put off by the unknown (purging, emesis, bloodletting) more than by the known. The page only names Abhyanga, Takradhara and herbal baths, while the hero image shows a dry powder rub.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician. The protocol is not stated anywhere on the site.

objectionGaps.question: How long before I see improvement, can it flare during treatment, and how long do results usually last? Will it come back?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Psoriasis is chronic and relapsing, so the realistic expectation decides the booking. The page offers only one 'life-changing' testimonial and no timeframe.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician. No figures may be invented, and any outcome statement needs sign-off.

objectionGaps.question: What will the total cost be for 14/21/28 nights, including internal medicines, lab tests and any Panchakarma?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page says medicines and tests 'can only be ascertained as your treatment progresses and will cost extra'. /faqs-downloads/ says medicines are included, and 'All-Inclusive, No hidden fees' says the opposite. An international patient paying 100% in advance needs a range.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs owner: one inclusion rule plus a typical medicine/test range for psoriasis. Nightly tariff is on this page; the rate-card validity conflicts with /faqs-downloads/.

objectionGaps.question: I am 55–70 with diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease, fatty liver or obesity (common alongside psoriasis). Is the programme safe for me, and is a doctor on site at night?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Comorbidities are common with psoriasis at this age. Purgation, heat and oil therapies raise real safety questions for these patients.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Partly on /faqs-downloads/ ('What considerations do you have for senior patients?': medical monitoring, emergency services on call, nearby hospital arrangements). Psoriasis- and comorbidity-specific safety needs physician.

objectionGaps.question: Who will be my physician, what are their qualifications, and do they speak English, German, French, Russian or Arabic?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The page says only 'Doctor might change as subject to availability' and 'multilingual staff'. Trust in a foreign doctor is the biggest barrier for a first-time Ayurveda patient.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Physician names and qualifications (BAMS) are on /online-consultation/, and 'Are Ayurvedic doctors real doctors?' is on /faqs-downloads/. The languages spoken need the owner (not stated anywhere).

objectionGaps.question: If it doesn't help, or I flare badly and need to leave early, do I get anything back?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: With 100% advance payment and 'Change in Date during Stay – No Refund', a patient with an unpredictable condition carries all the risk.
objectionGaps.answerSource: The refund rules are on this page and /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ (which has a force-majeure clause). Any medical-reason exception needs the owner.

objectionGaps.question: Is this a hospital or a holiday resort? The awards say 'Spa Resort' and 'Luxury'.
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: A patient comparing this with a dermatology clinic, or an insurer or visa officer, reads about 25 spa/luxury/resort award cards on a psoriasis page as a wellness holiday, which undermines both clinical trust and a medical visa.
objectionGaps.answerSource: This page: the NABH block (AH-2024-0250, valid to 24 Apr 2027). The owner should rule on moving hospitality awards off clinical pages.

objectionGaps.question: What does a psoriasis patient's actual day look like — how many therapies, oil left on the plaques, bathing, sun exposure?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The sample day and weekly activities are generic across programmes: one therapy slot, farm visits and cooking class, versus the '2 therapies per day' claim. Nothing is skin-specific.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician for a psoriasis-specific sample day.

objectionGaps.question: Which reports should I bring (blood tests, liver/kidney function if I'm on methotrexate, photos, dermatologist letter)?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: 'Bring… recent reports' is too vague to act on. The right tests help the physician decide suitability before the patient flies.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician.

objectionGaps.question: Can I get a medical visa, and will you send an invitation or medical letter?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Stays of 14–28+ nights. Patients from Russia, the Middle East and elsewhere need to know if a tourist e-Visa is enough or if a Medical/Medical Attendant visa is needed.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ ('What visa requirements should international patients be aware of?': invitation letter on request) and /how-to-reach/ ('Visa & entry', which links to the Government of India portal).

objectionGaps.question: Is the airport transfer included, and which airport should I fly to?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: This page lists 'Airport transfers' under Inclusions, while /faqs-downloads/ prices them as an extra cost. That surprises a patient at the point of booking.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /how-to-reach/ and /faqs-downloads/ (transfer fares). Note that the two pages give different airport distances (CJB 62 km vs 75 km). The owner must confirm included vs chargeable.

objectionGaps.question: Can my husband or wife come with me, and what does it cost? Does 'Double' mean two patients or a patient plus a companion?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Most 40–70 patients travel with a partner. The tariff shows Single/Double per night without saying whether both people are treated.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ ('Can a family member stay with me…': extra bed/meals). What the Double rate covers needs the owner.

objectionGaps.question: What happens after I go home — can I get my medicines abroad or through customs, and is online follow-up included?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Psoriasis needs long-term maintenance. Patients worry about running out of medicines, customs rules in the EU/US/Russia, and whether follow-up is free.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ ('How do I continue my Ayurvedic routine after returning home?': online follow-ups, medicines for purchase). Cost, frequency and shipping/customs need the owner.

objectionGaps.question: Are your medicines safe? Do they contain heavy metals or bhasmas, and where are they made?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Heavy-metal content in some Ayurvedic preparations is a common Western concern, and many dermatologists raise it with patients.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician/owner: the source and manufacturing standard of the formulations dispensed at KTAHV (not stated on this page).

objectionGaps.question: Should I book the Psoriasis programme or the Skin Vitality Revival programme?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: /treatment-for-skin-diseases/ also lists 'Eczema and psoriasis' and carries a psoriasis testimonial. Two overlapping pages with no stated difference split the decision and search intent, and neither links to the other.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs owner/physician to define the difference. Both pages exist in the prerender set.

objectionGaps.question: Will insurance pay for this?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: European and US patients expect a claim route. Knowing there is none, or only reimbursement, changes the budget.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ ('Are Ayurvedic treatments covered by insurance?': no cashless tie-ups; treatment summaries and medical certificates provided for reimbursement claims).

objectionGaps.question: What will I eat, and can you handle diabetic or gluten-free needs? Is dairy really excluded?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: The FAQ says 'avoiding dairy, red meat' while using buttermilk (Takradhara) and serving an all-vegetarian kitchen. A patient with comorbidities needs a clear, consistent answer.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician for the psoriasis diet. The vegetarian-only rule is on /cancellation-and-refund-policy/ and /faqs-downloads/.

objectionGaps.question: When is the best season to come for psoriasis — monsoon humidity or dry winter?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: International patients plan months ahead, and the climate affects psoriatic skin.
objectionGaps.answerSource: The general seasonal guide is on /faqs-downloads/ ('When is the best time to visit for specific treatments?'). A psoriasis-specific recommendation needs the physician.

objectionGaps.question: I have limited mobility or knee/joint pain (psoriatic arthritis). Are the villas and therapy rooms step-free?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Patients over 60 with psoriatic arthritis may not manage steps or getting on and off a treatment table.
objectionGaps.answerSource: /faqs-downloads/ (ramps, mobility assistance) and /how-to-reach/ (wheelchair-accessible vehicle). Villa-level step-free access needs the owner.

objectionGaps.question: Can I use the pool and shared areas with visible plaques, and is psoriasis a problem for other patients?
objectionGaps.whyItMatters: Visible psoriasis carries stigma. Patients worry about being stared at or excluded, and whether oiled skin and the pool mix.
objectionGaps.answerSource: Needs physician/owner.

clinicalRisk: 'The actual reason behind Psoriasis is yet to be known but it is said to be hereditary in nature.' This describes the cause of the disease and needs physician wording.

'The underlined reason can be considered to be the increase of pitta dosha in the body.' This gives a dosha cause for psoriasis. Classical texts treat Kushtha as tridoshic, and psoriasis is often correlated with Ekakushtha/Kitibha (vata-kapha).

'…has come up with a new and exceptional solution to your skin problems', together with 'Has it shown results even after going through courses of different types of medicines?', implies superiority over conventional treatment.
Benefits: 'Enhances skin health and decreases symptoms like scaling and itching'. This is a symptom-outcome claim.
'Improves vitality and strengthens the immune system' and 'Improved immunity and overall vitality' claim an immune-boosting effect in an immune-mediated disease.
'Balance restoration and prevention of further complications' and 'Prevents health issues by addressing the core cause' are prevention/root-cause claims.
FAQ 1: 14–28 days with 'For best results, the doctors may suggest a lengthier stay'. This needs a physician-set duration and must not imply outcomes.

FAQ 2: the named protocol (Abhyanga, Takradhara, medicated herbal baths, internal medicines, Panchakarma as needed). The physician must confirm the actual psoriasis protocol, and whether Udwarthana (hero image, sample day) is used on psoriatic skin.
FAQ 3: the diet rules ('excludes inflammatory items', 'avoiding dairy, red meat', diet 'based on their body composition'). This contradicts Takradhara (buttermilk) and needs physician correction.
FAQ 4 and 'Continuous post-discharge wellness plan': what home care, herbal remedies and follow-up are actually provided.
'Panchakarma, a comprehensive detoxification process, helps eliminate toxins from the body' (Process step 04).
'…continued doctor support for a safe and effective journey'. This is a safety and efficacy claim.

The indications list 'Patients with hormonal skin conditions' / 'Individuals with complex skin disorders', with no contraindications stated. The physician should define who is suitable and who is not (e.g. erythrodermic/pustular flares, pregnancy, patients on biologics).

The patient testimonial ('My skin felt calmer and less inflamed…', 'genuinely life-changing') under the heading 'Transformative Results'. This is an outcome claim for disease treatment; the owner must verify the testimonial's source and it needs physician/regulatory review before use.
The Sunday session 'prevent diseases naturally' and the 'Detoxifying Drink… kickstart the metabolism' lines. These are generic health claims repeated on a condition page.

Missing entirely: any statement on existing psoriasis medication (methotrexate, biologics, steroids) — whether to continue it or how to taper. This is the page's highest-risk gap and needs Dr. Deepu John's wording before it can be added.
verifyNotes:
I checked all 53 findings: 45 kept, 8 rejected.

How I checked: I pulled the visible text out of english-candidate/prerender/treatment-for-psoriasis.html and read the raw HTML for attributes. The snapshot contains only the page body (no meta tags, no JSON-LD). I compared the cross-page claims with the prerendered /faqs-downloads/, /cancellation-and-refund-policy/, /treatment-for-spondylitis/, /preventive-and-regenerative-treatment/ and /treatment-for-skin-diseases/ pages.

Kept, with evidence:
- Locked words appear word for word in the page's own copy (0-3, 16, 21, 24, 28, 33-36, 41-43).
- 46: the hero aria-label says "onto the back of a guest lying face-down…".
- 47: this quote is not in the body snapshot. It is the ogTitle for this route in english-candidate/route-manifest.json, and app/(english)/_families/metadata.ts uses that field, so the page really ships it (no space between the two titles). I kept it on that basis.
- 38: /faqs-downloads/ says the rates are valid "1 Oct 2026 – 30 Sep 2027"; this page says "April 1, 2025, to October 31, 2026".
- 25: /faqs-downloads/ lists airport/railway transfers as extra cost (Coimbatore ₹6,775 one way), but this page lists them under Inclusions.
- 39: the policy page says 50% applies "between 15 days and 30 days prior".
- 51: /faqs-downloads/ gives the 5-12 rule (50% for food and bedding), which this page's Child Policy leaves out.
- 50: /faqs-downloads/ gives extra meals "per night"; this page gives no unit.
- 7 and 8: this page says both "All-Inclusive… No hidden fees" and that medicines and tests "will cost extra". /faqs-downloads/ contradicts itself too: line 263 includes "Herbal medicines and formulations during your stay", while line 208 says they are "charged as needed".
- 15: the History paragraph is the same template as the spondylitis and preventive pages, with the programme name swapped.
- 52: /treatment-for-skin-diseases/ lists "Eczema and psoriasis" but is not among the related programmes here. This matters for the user's flow work.
- 4: I kept this only for the red-meat point, because the page itself says meals are "vegetarian or vegan". The Takradhara/dairy reasoning is weak: Takradhara uses buttermilk externally, which does not conflict with avoiding dairy in the diet.

Rejected:
- 5: "average… between 14 and 28" is a pedantic style point, and program vs programme is a spelling variant.
- 9: the sentence can be parsed; asking for follow-up details is about completeness, not an error.
- 26: dropping the article in a terse "Bring:" list is normal style.
- 27: "Bharathanatyam" is a common Indian transliteration.
- 29: "Do's and Don'ts on Ayurveda" is acceptable Indian English.
- 30: the daily routine is explicitly a "general outline", and classical Kushtha treatment does include udvartana, so there is no clear contradiction.
- 48: whether the programme covers hormonal skin conditions is a scope question for the physician, not a defect.
- 49: "practitioner" is not a banned or hospitality word.

Still to be decided by the physician or owner (Dr. Deepu John; flagged, not decided here): 13 and 14 (dosha and causation wording), 17-19 (immune, prevention and complication claims), 7 and 8 (whether medicines are included in the price), 38 (which rate card applies from 1 Oct 2026), 41 (NABH scope wording), 44 (whether hospitality award names may appear on clinical pages).
